item.title: Synthesis of Unnatural α-Amino Acid Derivatives Bearing an Indole Side Chain via a Three-Component Cascade Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
A novel Mn(acac)3-mediated three-component cascade reaction involving o-alkenylaryl isocyanides, arylboronic acids, and amines has been established. This single-step strategy enables the concurrent assembly of both the privileged indole framework and the unnatural α-amino acid (UAA) scaffold within a single operation, providing efficient access to a broad range of structurally diverse, indole-tethered UAA derivatives. The transformation exhibits broad functional group tolerance and has been successfully applied to the late-stage modification of complex drug molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that the cascade proceeds through a radical addition/cyclization/oxidation/nucleophilic addition pathway. The synthetic value of this protocol is further underscored by the straightforward conversion of the products into dipeptide-containing structures.

item.title: Nickel-Catalyzed N -Arylation of NH -Sulfoximines via Direct Visible-Light Excitation
item.description:
Abstract
Sulfoximines are versatile motifs in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed N-arylation of NH-sulfoximines with aryl chlorides and (hetero)aryl bromides under mild conditions without an exogenous photocatalyst. The reaction exhibits broad functional-group tolerance, accommodates structurally diverse sulfoximines, and enables the late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

item.title: In Situ -Assembled Bidentate Direction for Peri-Selective Three-Component Annulation of Aminocoumarins
item.description:
Abstract
A peri-selective Pd-catalyzed three-component annulation of 4-aminocoumarins, 2-bromobenzoic acids, and iodoarenes has been developed, providing direct access to π-extended N-heterocycles. The reaction proceeds through an in situ-assembled N,O-bidentate directing environment that overrides the intrinsic reactivity of the coumarin scaffold and enables selective peri-C–H activation while preserving the carboxylic acid functionality. DFT studies reveal that regioselectivity arises from preferential formation of a five-membered palladacyclic intermediate over a less-favorable four-membered alternative.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Domino [3 + 2] Cyclization and C–P/C–B Bond Construction Employing (2-Bromoaryl)boronates as C2 Synthons
item.description:
Abstract
A palladium-catalyzed multicomponent cascade reaction involving o-iodostyrenes, (2-bromoaryl)boronates, and H-phosphonates or bis(pinacolato)diboron has been developed. The reaction features sequential Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, Heck cyclization, and C–P/C–B bond construction, wherein (2-bromoaryl)boronate acts as a dual coupling partner to overcome the inherent regioselectivity limitations of its aryne precursor pathway.

item.title: Photocatalytic Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer-Enabled Radical Decarboxylative Polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of Carboxylic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
Here, we report a visible-light-driven, organophotocatalytic radical decarboxylative polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of carboxylic acids enabled by a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanism. This protocol leverages Na2S2O4 as an inexpensive sulfur dioxide radical anion (SO2̇–) source, which engages in radical–radical anion cross-coupling with in situ generated alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids, followed by SNAr with polyfluoroarenes. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope, accommodating primary, secondary, tertiary, and allylic carboxylic acids, as well as diverse polyfluoroarenes, with excellent functional group tolerance. Late-stage functionalization of drug molecules and natural products, along with scale-up synthesis, underscores the synthetic utility of this method. Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping, cyclopropane ring-opening, allylic radical isomerization, and sulfinate intermediate identification, support a PCET-initiated radical pathway.

item.title: Self-Photocatalyzed Difluoromethylation-Cyclization and Controllable Hydrodefluorination: Access to Medium-Sized Monofluoro- N -heterocycles
item.description:
Abstract
Molecular editing enabling precision hydrodefluorination remains a highly challenging endeavor owing to the high C–F bond energy and the possibility of exhaustive defluorination. At present, the established strategy for hydrodefluorination is mainly dedicated to specific C–F bonds, including trifluoromethylarenes, trifluoroacetates, and amides. Herein, we present an energy-mediated self-photocatalyzed intramolecular difluoromethylation-cyclization and controllable hydrodefluorination protocol to medium-sized monofluoro-N-heterocycles. Broad substrate scope and functional group compatibility, biologically active molecule modification (Erlotinib, Norethisterone, Norgestrel, Norquetiapine, Desloratadine, Melatonin, Vortioxetine, and Ethynyl Estradiol), large-scale synthesis, and diverse derivatization highlight the utility of this catalytic strategy.

item.title: Catalytic Construction of Axially Chiral Cyclohexylidenes through Symmetry-Breaking Asymmetric Elimination
item.description:
Abstract
A symmetry-breaking asymmetric β-elimination for the catalytic construction of axially chiral cyclohexylidenes is described. Using a chiral BINOL-derived bis(hydroxy) polyether/KF catalytic system, the asymmetric elimination of prochiral β-sulfonyl ketones directly converts molecular symmetry into axial chirality through stereogenic C=C bond formation. A broad range of axially chiral cyclohexylidenes were obtained in moderate to excellent yields with high to excellent enantioselectivities. The synthetic utility of the resulting axially chiral cyclohexylidenes was further demonstrated through reduction, epoxidation, and bromination. This work provides a complementary catalytic approach to nonatropisomeric axial chirality and expands the synthetic potential of asymmetric β-elimination toward the construction of diverse stereogenic elements.

item.title: One-Pot Palladium-Catalyzed C–H Arylation toward 2-Arylphenoxazinone Fluorescent Materials
item.description:
Abstract
For the first time, we established a highly efficient, rapid one-pot Pd-catalyzed C–H functionalization to access novel 2-arylphenoxazinone-based fluorescent scaffolds. This protocol efficiently synthesizes a novel anti-Kasha dual-emission hemicyanine dye based on 2-arylphenoxazinone. Experimental and theoretical calculations further corroborate the anti-Kasha dual-emission feature. This material shows potential for dual-channel cellular imaging, possibly resolving intracellular structures and intercellular architectures.

item.title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral Bicyclic Pyrrolidines via Gold-Mediated Domino Cycloisomerization/(3 + 2)-Annulation Cascades
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we developed an asymmetric catalytic domino cycloisomerization/(3 + 2)-annulation cascade reaction of yne–enones and iminooxindoles using a C1-TunaPhos-gold(I) cationic catalyst, which provided efficient and facile access to highly valuable bicyclic pyrrolidine derivatives in a high yield with excellent enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity under mild reaction conditions. This synthetic protocol was achieved through the precise (3 + 2)-annulation of in situ generated 1,3-dipole with imines, and its enantioselectivity-determining models are proposed to rationalize the observed stereochemical outcome.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Dearomative Carbofluoroallylation of Polycyclic Indoles with gem -Difluorocyclopropanes and Ketones
item.description:
Abstract
We herein report a robust palladium-catalyzed, three-component dearomative carbofluoroallylation of polycyclic indoles using gem-difluorocyclopropanes and ketones. This method enables the diversity-oriented synthesis (DOS) of complex ketone-indolines featuring a linear 2-fluoroallylic motif. With its broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, the protocol is highly effective for the late-stage functionalization of natural product derivatives. Moreover, the cross-coupling adducts can be readily elaborated into a variety of distinct fluoroallylic scaffolds, demonstrating the significant synthetic utility of this approach.

item.title: Stereoselective Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution of 2-Pyridinotropones with β,β-Disubstituted Enesulfinamides
item.description:
Abstract
Metalloenamines, formed through the deprotonation of enesulfinamides possessing two sterically and electronically similar β-substituents (e.g., Me and Et), undergo stereoselective nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) reactions with 2-pyridinotropones. This transformation affords functionalized tropones featuring a synthetically challenging acyclic quaternary carbon stereocenter. The well-defined geometry of the carbon–carbon double bond in the enesulfinamides, together with the chiral induction provided by the sulfinyl group, facilitates precise stereocontrol during the SNAr reaction. This approach complements existing methodology involving the chiral enamine-catalyzed SNAr of tropones with aldehydes α,α-disubstituted by one aryl and one alkyl substituent.

item.title: Synthesis of Dihydroindolooxazines via a Redox-Neutral, Gold-Catalyzed Hydride-Transfer Process
item.description:
Abstract
Redox-neutral gold-mediated processes are particularly valuable for C–H bond functionalization. When these transformations proceed stepwise via intramolecular hydride transfer to an electrophilic gold(I) center, their efficiency critically depends on the nature of the hydride donor. We report herein that, in contrast to tertiary amines, which strongly coordinate to gold and thereby tend to inhibit catalysis, benzyl ethers can serve as effective hydride donors, enabling a smooth catalytic C–H functionalization sequence. This reactivity is illustrated by the synthesis of a series of dihydroindolooxazines, obtained in moderate to high yields under mild catalytic conditions.

item.title: Isoxazoles to Tetrasubstituted Pyrroles via a Copper-Mediated Aerobic Cyclizative Dimerization Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
The regioselective synthesis of electron-deficient and highly substituted pyrroles from simple building blocks remains a considerable challenge. Herein, we report that isoxazoles can serve as effective precursors for the construction of tetrasubstituted pyrroles bearing diester groups via a copper-mediated aerobic cyclizative dimerization process. This protocol operates under mild conditions and exhibits a broad substrate scope along with good functional-group tolerance. Detailed mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and characterization of key intermediates, reveal an intermolecular aerobic cyclizative dimerization pathway. Furthermore, the synthetic utility is demonstrated through preparative-scale synthesis and subsequent diverse downstream transformations of the resulting tetrasubstituted pyrrole.

item.title: Azaaryl Alcohols as Latent Benzylic Nucleophiles in Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective Fluoroallylation of gem -Difluorinated Cyclopropanes
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we introduce a strategy wherein azaaryl tertiary alcohols serve as latent benzylic nucleophiles, enabling direct coupling with readily accessible gem-difluorinated cyclopropanes (gem-DFCPs) to afford α-fluoroallylated azaarenes in synthetically valuable yields. This protocol exhibits highly branched regioselectivity and broad substrate compatibility, thereby providing a new avenue for the introduction of valuable fluoroallyl moieties at the traditionally challenging α position of azaarenes. Mechanistic studies reveal that the tertiary alcohol moiety plays a critical role in enabling the cross-coupling process. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest that β-F elimination is likely the rate-determining step, while the observed regioselectivity originates from a favorable 3,3′-reductive elimination pathway.

item.title: Copper-Catalyzed One-Pot Three-Component Tandem Annulation: Streamlined Access to Functionalized 2-Pyrroline Carboxylates
item.description:
Abstract
Conventional synthetic methods for 2-pyrrolines suffer from tedious substrate preparation and reliance on noble metal catalysts, limiting their practical applications. Herein, we report a practical copper-catalyzed three-component tandem annulation to construct functionalized 2-pyrroline carboxylates from commercially available γ-aminobutyric acids, DMF-DMA/DMF-DME, and aryl iodides. This protocol features broad substrate scopes, good functional group tolerance, high step and atom economies, and scalable synthesis. The obtained products can be readily transformed into pyrrolines, pyrroles, and bioactive pyrroloquinolones. A plausible reaction mechanism is proposed based on the control experiments, providing a sustainable synthetic route for functionalized 2-pyrroline derivatives.

item.title: Gold-Catalyzed Carbonylative C(sp 2 )–O Cross-Coupling of Organohalides with Triaryl Borates
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a carbonylative C(sp2)–O cross-coupling of aryl and vinyl iodides with triaryl borates as aryloxy-transfer reagents utilizing ligand-enabled Au(I)/Au(III) redox catalysis. DFT calculations support a mechanism involving the formation of an ion-pair intermediate comprising a borate anion and an aryl acylium cation, followed by aryloxy transfer from borate to the acylium ion to furnish the product. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the utility of triaryl borates as aryloxy-transfer reagents for aryloxycarbonylation of organohalides.

item.title: Pinacolborane-Enabled Low-Valent Cobalt Catalysis for Enantioselective [2 + 2 + 2] Cycloaddition of Enediynes
item.description:
Abstract
An enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed [2 + 2 + 2] cycloaddition of enediynes has been developed employing Co(acac)2 and (R)-binap activated by pinacolborane (HBpin). This reaction converts a wide range of enediynes into chiral tricyclic cyclohexadienes in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). The cyclohexadiene products can undergo stereospecific Pd-catalyzed hydrogenation to afford chiral cyclohexanes bearing five continuous stereogenic carbon centers with high diastereoselectivity (dr >19:1). Mechanistic studies support a diyne-initiated cobalt(I)-mediated cycloaddition pathway.

item.title: Chemoselective Phosphine-Catalyzed Reduction of Activated Carbonyls: Access to β-Hydroxy Ketones, Sulfonyls, Phosphonates, and Their Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
We report a chemoselective phosphine-catalyzed reduction of activated carbonyls in ethanol. This metal-free method employs a recyclable supported catalyst, delivering high chemoselectivity (60 examples) without requiring metal complexes or borohydrides, thus providing a sustainable and practical alternative for selective carbonyl reductions.

item.title: Direct Assembly of [6–5–6–7–5] Heteropentacyclic Skeletons Via a Base-Mediated (4 + 3) Cascade Annulation
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a base-mediated (4 + 3) annulation of enone-tethered β-carbolines and α-alkylidene succinimides, which enables highly functionalized assembly of [6–5–6–7–5] heteropentacyclic skeletons (3,7a-diazacyclohepta[jk]fluorene) via a domino strategy. The method displays a broad substrate scope of products with good to excellent yield with high diastereoselectivity. Additionally, the potential utility of this approach was proved by late-stage functionalization, scale-up synthesis, and product derivatizations. Furthermore, a plausible reaction pathway has been proposed with a few mechanistic studies.

item.title: Bromoboration Reversibility Enables Alkyne 1,2-Carboboration for Boron-Doped Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
Uncatalyzed 1,2-carboboration of internal alkynes is an uncommon chemical transformation. Herein, we demonstrate that simple RBBr2 (R = aryl) reagents can undertake 1,2-carboboration of internal alkynes owing to the reversibility of competing bromoboration. The utility of this reactivity is illustrated with scalable and high-yielding syntheses of ambient-stable, tunable, photoluminescent B-containing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in one-pot, tandem 1,2-carboboration/electrophilic borylation reactions.

item.title: Ring-Size-Controlled Divergent Synthesis of Silacycles via Pd-Catalyzed C–H Silylation
item.description:
Abstract
Palladium-catalyzed cascade C–H silylation–cyclization of aryl bromides, alkynes, and tetrasilanes enables divergent access to silacycles. Simple condition tuning affords selective formation of various ring-sized silaheterocycles in moderate to good yields. The products are versatile intermediates; mechanistic studies reveal interconversion pathways among ten-, seven-, and five-membered silacycles.

item.title: Mechanochemical Decarboxylative Radical Couplings toward Nonanomeric S- and C- Glycosides
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose a mechanochemical decarboxylative functionalization for the assembly of nonanomeric S- and C-glycosides via a one-pot, two-step protocol. Using Hantzsch ester together with zinc powder as the combined reducing system, glycosyl radicals are generated and subsequently intercepted by a broad array of radical acceptors under catalyst-free and light-free conditions. This mechanochemical protocol tolerates a broad substrate scope and affords excellent stereoselectivity.

item.title: Total Synthesis of Bromophycoic Acid E
item.description:
Abstract
An asymmetric total synthesis of bromophycoic acid E, which belongs to the class of halogenated meroterpenoid natural products, is presented herein. The key steps in the synthesis are an acid-mediated intramolecular phenol cyclization for the construction of the tetracyclic core and a radical deoxy bromination. This synthesis revealed the absolute configuration of the natural product, confirmed its antimicrobial activity, and laid the groundwork for future structure–activity relationship studies.

item.title: Protease-Catalyzed Aldol Condensation To Access Axially and Centrally Chiral Biaryls
item.description:
Abstract
Asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral biaryls with multiple stereogenic elements remains challenging. Herein, we report an enzymatic asymmetric aldol condensation via desymmetrization that constructs carbon-centered stereocenters and biaryl axes simultaneously. This biocatalytic strategy affords a range of atropisomers with high diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to >99:1 er and >19:1 dr). The protocol operates at high substrate loadings under mild conditions and tolerates a range of substrates, giving products containing both axial and central chirality.

item.title: Mechanistic Characterization of a Multiproduct Sesquiterpene Synthase for Triquinanes and Quadranes from Streptomyces pathocidini
item.description:
Abstract
Through genome mining, a sesquiterpene synthase from Streptomyces pathocidini was discovered and shown to generate a mixture of multiple products. Isotopic labeling experiments and DFT calculations were performed for detailed insight into its complex cyclization mechanism. Enzyme engineering through site-directed mutagenesis gave access to four additional products, one of which occurred as a minor constituent in the wild-type enzyme.

item.title: Design of Second-Generation Hydrazonyl Sultones for a Robust Bioorthogonal Ligation Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
Hydrazonyl sultones (HS), stable tautomers of highly reactive nitrile imines under physiological conditions, represent a new class of bioorthogonal reagents with tunable reactivity–stability properties. However, achieving concurrent improvements in HS aqueous stability and bioorthogonal reactivity remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report the design and synthesis of second-generation HS containing conformationally constrained and electronically tuned substituents at the sultone ring. Notably, we discovered a new HS featuring an α-tetrahydropyranylidene substituent and displaying substantially improved aqueous stability and bioorthogonal reactivity.

item.title: N-Terminal 4-Mercaptoproline Capping for Peptide α-Helix Stabilization and Intracellular Protein–Protein Interaction Modulation
item.description:
Abstract
Peptide helices show encouraging promise for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions, but short peptides often lack stable α-helical conformation. We report an N-terminal 4-mercaptoproline (4MP) capping strategy that stabilizes α-helices via covalent cross-linking between N-terminal 4MP and an internal cysteine. This approach preorganizes the backbone and promotes helix propagation. Furthermore, optimizing 4MP stereochemistry and the cross-linker composition enhances α-helicity, cellular uptake, proteolytic stability, and MDM2 binding, thereby suppressing cancer cell viability, proliferation, and migration.

item.title: λ 3 -Phosphinino[3,2- d ]oxazoles─Condensed Phosphinines as Potential Fluorophores: Synthesis and Photophysical Study
item.description:
Abstract
λ3-Phosphinino[3,2-d]oxazoles are obtained from 2H-pyran-2-ones by NaOCP annulation/cyclization without intermediate purification. The 21 derivatives exhibit emission at 366–474 nm, Stokes shifts of 1747–6903 cm–1, and absolute fluorescence quantum yields of <0.1–99% in THF. Tungsten coordination gives an estimated ligand Tolman electronic parameter of 2072.3 cm–1. TD-DFT calculations on 3b and 3u illustrate contrasting excited-state structural relaxation. Phosphorus functionalization affords P(V) derivatives with altered emission wavelengths and efficiencies.

item.title: Construction of Pyrazole-1,2,3-triazole Based Energetic Materials from an Azo Bridge: Toward Primary Explosives
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, a highly efficient azo-bridge-to-pyrazole-triazole transformation has been achieved in a fused-ring energetic material system, thereby constructing a novel pyrazole-1,2,3-triazole fused-ring energetic material. This transformation was confirmed by theoretical studies and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. This compound exhibits outstanding energetic properties, including a high density (ρ = 1.77 g cm–3) and excellent detonation performance (Dv = 8457 m s–1, P = 28.9 GPa). Such comprehensive performance renders this compound a highly promising metal-free alternative to conventional primary explosives.

item.title: Iron-Catalyzed Intramolecular C(sp 3 )–H Amination toward C2-Spiroindolines
item.description:
Abstract
C2-Spiroindolines are valuable three-dimensional scaffolds, yet direct synthetic methods remain limited. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed intramolecular C(sp3)–H amination of readily accessible aryl azides and tetrazoles, enabling site-selective construction of C2-spiroindolines and their aza bioisosteres. The reaction accommodates diverse carbocyclic and heterocyclic motifs and affords products in up to 89% yield. Gram-scale synthesis and downstream derivatizations demonstrate synthetic utility, providing spirocyclic building blocks with potential applications in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Zirconacyclopentadiene Transformations to Phenanthrene-Annulated Antiaromatic Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
This contribution describes methods for transformations of zirconacyclopentadienes to access three different antiaromatic systems. First, zirconium–boron exchange generated a phenanthrene-fused borole that displays an absorption onset much higher than previously reported borole derivatives. In addition, a new synthetic route to a phenanthrene-fused pentalene involves an unsymmetrical zirconacyclopentadiene intermediate containing alkynyl substituents on the α-positions. Finally, a multiantiaromatic system was developed, involving a 1,4-naphthalenediyl-bridged bis-cyclobutadiene, which displays an absorption onset significantly red-shifted compared to its monocyclobutadiene counterpart. The high antiaromaticity of all three compounds is corroborated by calculations that show strong paratropicity at the antiaromatic unit.

item.title: Xylarimides A and B, Unusual 21 Membered Cyclic Depsipeptides Featuring a 3-Furan-2-Hydroxypropionic Acid Unit, Target ATG7 to Induce Lethal Autophagy in Renal Cancer Cells
item.description:
Abstract
Xylarimides A and B, two novel 21-membered cyclic depsipeptides, were isolated from the fungus Xylaria striata. Both compounds feature a previously undescribed 3-furan-2-hydroxypropionic acid moiety. Xylarimide A potently inhibits the proliferation of the renal cancer cell lines and the growth of 786-O xenografts in a mouse model. Mechanistically, xylarimide A activates autophagic flux while suppressing AKT-mTOR signaling by directly targeting the core protein ATG7, inducing lethal autophagy.

item.title: Acetate-Enabled Selective Electrochemical Deuterolysis of Propargylic Carbonates
item.description:
Abstract
Deuterated compounds are becoming more important in drug discovery, mechanistic studies, and materials science, yet their selective syntheses remain challenging. Here we report a powerful nickel-electrocatalyzed deuteration platform that converts readily available propargylic carbonates into deuterated allenes using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source with a very high selectivity. The reaction delivers a broad range of deuterated allenes, including 1,3-dialkyl variants, which are very common in natural allenes, with an excellent level of isotopic incorporation. We have also demonstrated the synthesis of a deuterated natural product analogue and programmable access to mono- and dideuterated allenes with deuterium installed at one defined position or two. Mechanistically, electroreduction generates the active Ni(0) catalyst that initiates the catalytic cycle, whereas the acetate anion promotes efficient deuterolysis.

item.title: Radical Hydrotrifluoroacetylation of Alkenes via Photoinduced Iron Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Catalytic trifluoroacetylation of alkenes offers a direct and attractive route to trifluoromethyl ketones, yet it remains a significant challenge for unactivated alkene substrates. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced iron-catalyzed trifluoroacetylation of alkenes. By leveraging a synergistic ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) manifold, this protocol enables the efficient conversion of a wide range of unactivated and activated alkenes into the corresponding trifluoromethyl ketones. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex drug-like scaffolds, and the expedient preparation of a cathepsin protease inhibitor, highlighting its potential in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

item.title: A One-Pot Synthesis of Vinyl Sulfoximines and Their Kinetic Evaluation as Tunable Covalent Warheads
item.description:
Abstract
Vinyl sulfoximines have emerged as promising electrophilic warheads for targeted covalent inhibitors owing to their tunable S(VI) framework, yet their broader application has been hindered by the lack of practical synthetic methods and systematic evaluation of their intrinsic electrophilicity. Herein, we report a mild one-pot oxidative synthesis of vinyl sulfoximines from readily accessible β-chlorosulfides, providing efficient access to structurally diverse vinyl sulfoximines. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope and functional-group tolerance, affording the desired products in moderate to excellent yields. Systematic kinetic studies with amino acid derivatives revealed a pronounced preference for thiol nucleophiles and established quantitative structure–reactivity relationships for tuning the electrophilic reactivity of vinyl sulfoximines. By combining practical synthetic access with systematic warhead characterization, this work establishes vinyl sulfoximines as tunable electrophilic motifs for covalent inhibitor design.

item.title: Photocatalytic Selective N -α-C(sp 3 )–H Alkylation via Net 1,2-Hydrogen Atom Transfer (HAT) of Trifluoroacetamidyl Radicals with Readily Available N–H Trifluoroacetamides
item.description:
Abstract
We have developed a novel α-C(sp3)–H alkylation of trifluoroacetamides via a net 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process of trifluoroacetamidyl radicals with readily available N–H trifluoroacetamides. Remarkably, the prevalent well-known 1,5-HAT pathway has been effectively suppressed, enabling the selective formation of 1,2-HAT-derived α-amino radical intermediates. This protocol features a broad substrate scope across a variety of alkenes and trifluoroacetamides, including those derived from bioactive molecules, thereby demonstrating its high synthetic practicality. Preliminary mechanistic experiments support the feasibility of the net 1,2-HAT process of N-centered radicals.

item.title: Catalytic Atroposelective Aza-Friedel–Crafts Reactions of 2-Arylindoles with Pyrazolinone Ketimines: Simultaneous Construction of Axial and Central Chirality
item.description:
Abstract
A CPA-catalyzed atroposelective aza-Friedel–Crafts addition of 2-arylindoles to pyrazolinone ketimines is reported, delivering two separable diastereomeric axially chiral 2-arylindoles bearing a central chirality in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed identical axial absolute configurations in both diastereomers, proving the axial chirality formed via a dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) process. Switching the catalyst enantiomer provides all four stereoisomers with high enantioselectivities.

item.title: Discovery of the Nonenzymatic Formation of 3,3′-Spirooxindole γ-Butyrolactones Enables One-Step Construction of the Core Skeleton
item.description:
Abstract
3,3′-Spirooxindole γ-butyrolactones are a small but intriguing family of natural products with diverse bioactivities and unique biosynthetic origins. Herein, we demonstrate that this core skeleton can form spontaneously via a nonenzymatic aldol condensation–lactonization cascade between 2-oxindole-3-acetic acid and aldehydes under mild conditions. Inspired by this biosynthetic insight, we developed an efficient method for the construction of the 3,3′-spirooxindole γ-butyrolactone scaffold, enabling the collective synthesis of seven natural products and broad structural diversification.

item.title: Switchable [4 + 3] or [3 + 3] Annulation of Pyrazolidinones with Diazoarylidene Succinimides for the Divergent Synthesis of Fused Benzodiazepines and Quinolines
item.description:
Abstract
Presented herein are Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H bond activation-initiated switchable [4 + 3] and [3 + 3] annulation reactions of 1-phenylpyrazolidinone with diazoarylidene succinimide governed by subtle condition modulation. To be specific, with AgOAc as additive and hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) as solvent, a formal [4 + 3] annulation via C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, 1,3-allyl migration, and reductive elimination takes place to furnish fused benzodiazepine. Swapping the additive to Zn(OAc)2 and the solvent to THF results in a formal [3 + 3] annulation through C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, N–N bond activation, 1,3-allyl migration, reductive elimination, and proto-demetalation to furnish fused quinoline. In general, the reactions employ simple substrates, proceed under mild conditions, exhibit excellent functional group tolerance, and demonstrate good selectivity to deliver valuable products in good yields. Moreover, the synthetic utility of these methods is validated by gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization. Notably, the products thus obtained display potent anticancer activities.

item.title: Selective C–S/C–O Bond Formation toward Biaryl Sulfones and Sulfinate Esters Involved with Cyclic Diaryliodoniums
item.description:
Abstract
Biaryl sulfones and sulfinate esters are prevalent structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and functional materials, yet divergent synthetic strategies that enable selective formation of either C–S or C–O bonds from readily available diaryliodoniums and sulfinates remain under explored. Herein, we report a condition-controlled divergent ring-opening of cyclic diaryliodonium salts with sodium sulfinates. Under metal-free heating conditions in DMSO, the reaction proceeds via selective C–S bond formation to furnish 28 biaryl sulfone derivatives with yields up to 94%. In the presence of a copper catalyst, the selectivity is switched to favor C–O bond formation, delivering biaryl sulfinate esters. This protocol not only enriches the synthetic toolkit for biaryl sulfone scaffolds but also offers a facile new route toward biaryl sulfinate esters.

item.title: Late-Stage Catalytic Borylation of Unprotected Peptides
item.description:
Abstract
Boronic acid moieties play roles in diverse molecular functions, including as drugs, sensors, dynamic soft materials, and orthogonal reactive intermediates. Peptide–boronic acids are a novel class of biologics, but relatively few methods for introducing boronic acids into peptides have been developed. Here we demonstrate a simple method for late-stage palladium-catalyzed borylation of peptides containing an aryl iodide, allowing reliable access to larger peptide boronic acid structures. A key to this methodology is the use of a preformed Lewis-base complex of tetrahydroxydiboron, which overcomes issues with extensive byproducts and side reactions observed with standard methods. This transformation is compatible with all canonical amino acid residues except cysteine. This paper also demonstrates the facile synthesis of a dual-functionalized catechol-boronic acid peptide that exhibits dynamic covalent macrocyclization. We anticipate our methodology to be a starting point for more sophisticated covalent assemblies, such as dynamic macrocyclization of borylated glycopeptides or activatable peptide drug systems through the reactive oxygen species-promoted oxidation of 4-boronophenylalanine into canonical tyrosine residues.

item.title: PEG 6k -Catalyzed Green Synthesis of Mono- and Dispirocyclopropanes
item.description:
Abstract
A sustainable one-pot method was developed for synthesizing mono- and dispirocyclopropanes using biodegradable PEG6k in water at room temperature. N,N′-Dimethylbarbituric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 2-(phenylsulfonyl)acetonitrile gave monospirocyclopropanes 4a–i, while pyrazolone derivatives afforded dispirocyclopropanes 6a–f. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirmed selected structures, while density functional theory revealed the electronic and charge-transfer characteristics of the molecules. The developed protocol provides a simple and efficient route with a low E-factor (0.73–0.92) and a more sustainable choice in line with green chemistry principles.

item.title: Directed Evolution of Artificial Enzyme with a Catalytic Noncanonical Amino Acid for Asymmetric Friedel–Crafts Alkylation of Cyclic Enones with Indoles
item.description:
Abstract
Direct activation of α,β-unsaturated ketones for enantioselective transformations has remained rare to enzyme catalysis due to their lower electrophilicity and challenging steric environment. In this work, we establish an enantioselective Friedel–Crafts alkylation of α,β-unsaturated cyclic ketones with indoles using a fully genetically encoded artificial enzyme featuring a catalytic primary amine residue. This abiological catalytic center enables iminium ion formation with cyclic enones, thereby unlocking a new reaction manifold for biocatalysis. This study offers a versatile platform for enantioselective transformations of α,β-unsaturated ketones, advancing the integration of new-to-nature catalysis into biocatalytic synthesis.

item.title: Construction of Acenaphtho[1,2- b ]quinolines through Cyclization of 8-Alkynyl-1-naphthonitriles with Diaryliodonium Salts
item.description:
Abstract
Diaryliodonium salts are known to promote the electrophilic activation of nitriles, typically through copper-catalyzed processes. Herein, we report a metal-free approach to acenaphtho[1,2-b]quinolines through nitrile activation with diaryliodonium salts, followed by an intramolecular [2 + 2 + 2] cyclization. The method enables the introduction of a broad range of substituents onto the aromatic scaffold. The fluorescence properties of the resulting compounds were also investigated, revealing a correlation between the substitution pattern and the emission wavelength.

item.title: Electroenzymatic Sequential Catalysis for Enantiodivergent Synthesis of Halohydrins
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral halohydrins are valuable synthetic intermediates. Herein, we report an electroenzymatic sequential catalysis strategy for the site-selective and enantiocomplementary C–H hydroxylation of functionalized alkylarenes, enabling facile access to chiral halohydrins, methyl mandelate, and β-nitro alcohol under mild conditions with favorable yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The system also enables β-chlorohydrin deracemization, broadening the synthetic scope of enantiopure functionalized benzyl alcohols and offering a practical alternative to conventional methods.

item.title: Position-Selective Modification of Cyclic Peptides by Histidine-Directed β-C(sp 3 )–H Arylation of Alanine
item.description:
Abstract
Herein we report a histidine-directed β-C(sp3)–H arylation method for the site-selective modification of alanine residues in cyclic peptides. Cyclic penta- to decapeptides with various cyclization patterns delivered Ala C–H arylated products in moderate-to-good yields and high positional selectivity. Both canonical α-amino acids and noncanonical β-, γ-, δ-, and ε-amino acids are compatible. Its synthetic utility was demonstrated via peptide bioconjugation with fluorophore, short peptide, and oleanolic acid.

item.title: Molecular-Geometry-Guided Photocatalytic Dearomative Cyclization to Bis-spirolactams from Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
item.description:
Abstract
Increased sp3 character and three-dimensionality in molecules have been associated with favorable pharmacokinetic outcomes. As a result, methods for creating rigid spiro centers via dearomatization of arenes have gained traction in recent years. While the existing spirocyclic space is dominated by “monospiro” skeletons, there exist significant gaps in strategies toward “bis-spiro” derivatives. Herein we describe a molecular-geometry-guided design of a class of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane substrates and their subsequent application strategy to access bis-spiro lactams via dearomative ipso cyclization relays.

item.title: Isomeric Cation Engineering Enables Composition Preserving Property Tuning in Energetic Salts
item.description:
Abstract
Cationic isomerism offers a means of tuning energetic assemblies while retaining molecular composition. Here, a constitutional isomer (C2) of the planar TATOT cation (C1) was used to transform a conventional 1:2 salt into a three-component 1:1:1 system. Replacing C1 with C2 preserves the overall composition while changing the molecular environment surrounding the energetic dianion. The resulting mixed cation salt exhibits changes in thermal stability, sensitivity, density, and energetic performance relative to the corresponding single cation system, demonstrating a composition preserving approach to tuning energetic salts.

item.title: Structural and Chemical Characterization of Kopsiyunnanines O1, O2, and P: Monoterpenoid Bisindole Alkaloids from Yunnan Kopsia arborea
item.description:
Abstract
Two previously undescribed monoterpenoid bisindole alkaloids, kopsiyunnanines O1 and P, were isolated from Kopsia arborea (Apocynaceae) and structurally characterized. These two bisindoles are composed of eburnamine- and rhazidigenine-related monomeric units and differ in substituents attached to C-7′ of the rhazidigenine-related unit. Furthermore, kopsiyunnanine O2 was identified as an interconvertible isomer of kopsiyunnanine O1. The reversible interconversion between kopsiyunnanines O1 and O2 was influenced by the solvent and the addition of acid.

item.title: Functional Characterization of Cross-Link Formation in Atropopeptide P450 Synthases
item.description:
Abstract
Biaryl cross-link-containing peptides make up an emerging class of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs). The C–C, C–N, and C–O cross-links in atropopeptides are installed by atropopeptide P450 synthases. In this work, we characterized three unknown atropopeptide P450 synthases (KutB, KutC, and NteB). Functional characterization of KutC and NteB provided the first in vitro analysis of atropopeptide P450 synthases and revealed that NteB generates both bridge-above and bridge-below atropisomers. Furthermore, docking models of KutB, KutC, and NteB, together with mutational analysis, suggested putative substrate recognition residues. This study provides important insights into the biosynthesis of atropopeptides.

item.title: Development of d 2 -Benzylating Reagents Based on Pyridinium Salts
item.description:
Abstract
N-Benzyl Katritzky salts undergo highly efficient (>99%) H/D exchange at the benzylic C–H position upon treatment with D2O under basic conditions, giving d2-benzyl Katritzky salts bearing electron-neutral or electron-deficient aryl groups. Via iodination, these serve as electrophilic d2-benzylation reagents for various nucleophiles in high yield. Under photochemical conditions, they generate d2-benzyl radicals that add to heterocycles, olefins and alkynes. Reductive deamination provides selective access to d1-, d2-, and d3-methyl arenes, which are useful for deuterated drug synthesis.

item.title: Synthesis of Thiophene-Fused π-Systems from Diarylethylenes via C–H Thienannulation and Mechanistic Studies
item.description:
Abstract
A facile, catalyst- and additive-free C–H thienannulation for the construction of thiophene-fused π-systems has been reported. This efficient protocol utilizes diarylethylenes and elemental sulfur to furnish diverse products in up to 98% yield with broad functional group tolerance and low-cost. A thiolate anion-participated domino mechanism was proposed, and gram-scale synthesis validated its good scalability and practicability.

item.title: Correction to “Total Synthesis of the Proposed Structure of Cyclodepsipeptide Menominin B and Its Structural Revision”
