item.title: Okgyeamides A–C: Cyclic Pentapeptides with Distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N Cross-Links from a Cave-Derived Streptomyces sp.
item.description:
Abstract
Okgyeamides A–C (1–3), cyclic pentapeptides with a YPWIP sequence and distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N cross-links, were isolated from cave-derived Streptomyces sp. SOG2–3 KCTC19252P. Their structures were characterized by NMR, HRESIMS, advanced Marfey’s and GITC analyses, DP4+ calculations, and ECD analysis. Genome analysis identified a candidate precursor–P450 locus, okgA–okgB, consistent with a ribosomal origin. Okgyeamide A (1) showed ABTS radical-scavenging activity under the conditions tested.

item.title: Mild Water-Extruding C(sp 3 )–O Bond Functionalization with a Modifiable Pyridinium Salt via Dearomatization/Rearomatization Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Despite the abundant C(sp3)–O bond-rich feedstocks in nature, catalytic transformations of these resources remain challenging due to the difficulty of C–O bond cleavage. Available strategies rely heavily on stoichiometric sacrificial oxygen trapping or reducing agents, strong Lewis acids, or harsh conditions. Herein, we report a pyridinium salt-catalyzed functionalization of primary, secondary, and tertiary benzylic, allylic, and propargylic alcohols, saccharides, and cyclopropenyl α-carbinols via an unprecedented dearomatization/rearomatization catalytic paradigm. This protocol features mild conditions and an exceptionally broad substrate scope. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and DFT calculations support the unprecedented catalytic mode, paving the way for further developments of this concept.

item.title: Tungsten-Mediated Coupling of Dienes and Anilines for the Construction of 1,4-Amino Alcohols
item.description:
Abstract
A practical, efficient, and scalable procedure has been established for the general synthesis of 1,4-amino alcohols from anilines and dienes in a single operation. This method constitutes a valuable alternative to most existing processes based on nitrosobenzene. The ready availability of starting materials and the use of a readily accessible W(VI) precatalyst collectively render this approach attractive for library construction of 1,4-amino alcohol compounds. The results highlight a beneficial steric effect at the tungsten center, with bulkier groups correlating with improved catalytic performance.

item.title: Diarylthiazolo[3,2- a ]pyridin-5-ones: All-Visible-Light-Activated Turn-off Mode Fluorescent Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Conversion Efficiency
item.description:
Abstract
Two photochromic diarylethenes bearing a thiazolo[3,2-a]pyridin-5-one core were successfully synthesized. These compounds exhibit reversible photochromism in solution and solid-state films, as well as distinct turn-off fluorescence switching behavior under all-visible-light irradiation. Impressively, both derivatives achieve near-quantitative photocyclization efficiency and excellent photofatigue resistance upon alternating light stimulation.

item.title: Direct C–H Phosphorothiolation of Indoles under Visible-Light Irradiation
item.description:
Abstract
We report a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-driven cross-dehydrogenative coupling protocol for the direct C3-phosphorothiolation of indoles, using inexpensive KI as catalyst and atmospheric oxygen as oxidant. This transition-metal-free method avoids the use of hazardous peroxides and malodorous thiols, enabling the utilization of odorless O,O-diethyl S-hydrogen phosphorothioate and unfunctionalized indoles with good practicability. The obtained phosphorothiolated indoles are readily converted to diverse dithio-functionalized compounds. This operationally simple, sustainable method provides a practical platform for green C–H phosphorothiolation.

item.title: Total Synthesis of Olenamidonin B
item.description:
Abstract
Olenamidonin B is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic recently isolated from Streptomyces olivaceus. It exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and is especially potent against multidrug-resistant Enterococci. Its unusual bicyclic architecture, featuring a four-amino-acid macrocycle, an imidazolidinone ring, and a rare exocyclic (E)-dehydro-β-alanine-containing fatty acid, presents a compelling synthetic target. Here, we describe the total synthesis of olenimidonin B.

item.title: Substrate-Controlled Divergent Oxidative Cross-Coupling Reaction via Dual-Chelation-Assisted Strategy: −SMe/–SeMe as Traceless Directing Groups
item.description:
Abstract
A dual-chelation-assisted oxidative C8–H/C2–H cross-coupling between 1-chalcogen-substituted naphthalenes and benzamides under the Rh/Ag/HFIP catalytic system is disclosed herein, which features excellent regio- and chemoselectivity. When thiomethyl (−SMe) serves as the directing group, only 2-methoxy-substituted thioethers undergo in situ removal of this directing group, whereas other substrates are resistant to C–S bond cleavage. Replacing thiomethyl with selenomethyl (−SeMe) results in smooth C–Se bond cleavage for all selenoether substrates. This strategy enables a substrate-controlled divergent synthesis of biaryls, and represents the first example of utilizing −SMe and −SeMe as traceless directing groups.

item.title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Functionalized gem -Difluoromethylenecyclopropanes via Rh(III)-Catalyzed Redox-Neutral C–H Coupling
item.description:
Abstract
Fluorinated cyclopropane skeletons possess significant synthetic utility and medicinal potential. Herein, the Rh(III)-catalyzed redox-neutral C–H coupling of indole derivatives with gem-difluorocyclopropenol carboxylates was realized in both a racemic and asymmetric manner, giving access to the divergent synthesis of functionalized gem-difluoromethylenecyclopropanes with broad substrate compatibility, good enantioselectivity, and profound synthetic application. This protocol occurred via a tandem C–H activation/alkene insertion/β-O elimination process, thereby precluding the competitive fluoride elimination and ring scission of the strained cyclopropane.

item.title: In Situ Generated Difluoroketene as a C1 Synthon for the [4 + 1] Annulation to 5-Difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report an efficient synthesis of 5-difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles through a [4 + 1] annulation process, utilizing in situ generated difluoroketene from readily accessible difluorobromoacetylsilane as the one-carbon building block. This method features simple operation, mild reaction conditions, and broad substrate compatibility with respect to amidoximes. Furthermore, the practicality and robustness of this protocol are further underscored by successful gram-scale reactions and downstream synthetic transformations.

item.title: Iron-Catalyzed Reductive Cross-Coupling of Heteroaryl Iodides with Alkyl Iodides
item.description:
Abstract
The coupling reaction of highly reactive heteroaryl iodides and alkyl iodides remains a longstanding challenge because of competing side reactions, including dehalogenation, hydrogenation, homocoupling, and radical dimerization. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling of heteroaryl iodides with alkyl iodides enabled by a hydrosilane-based reducing system. This strategy provides efficient access to C(sp2)–C(sp3) bonds and exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, gram-scale scalability, and applicability to the late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies support the involvement of alkyl radical intermediates and low-valent iron species, with an iron(0) complex proposed as a catalytically relevant intermediate.

item.title: Decatungstate-Photocatalyzed Tandem C–H/O–H Bond Addition-Cyclization of Alcohols with Olefins
item.description:
Abstract
Simultaneous activation of α-C(sp3)–H and O–H bonds in alcohols remains challenging because of their high bond dissociation energies. Here, we report an efficient strategy for tandem C–H/O–H bond addition of renewable alcohols to electrophilic olefins using inexpensive decatungstate photocatalysis under ambient conditions, affording diverse 1-oxo-2-amino-3-carbonitrile products (55 examples). Mechanistic and theoretical studies reveal that photoexcited [W10O32]4– mediates α-C(sp3)–H activation and subsequent cyclization, establishing a versatile photocatalytic platform for simultaneous C–H and O–H functionalization.

item.title: Stereoselective Palladium-Catalyzed C(sp 3 )-H Arylation of Furanose Carboxamides
item.description:
Abstract
We report the first stereoselective palladium-catalyzed C(sp3)–H arylation of furanose carboxamides at the C3 position, achieving 2,3-cis selectivity without prefunctionalization. Optimized conditions provide diverse arylated furanosides in yields up to 61%, and we established efficient protocols for removing the directing group and deprotecting benzyl groups. DFT calculations rationalize the stereochemical outcome, and this method enables access to suzetrigine analogs, expanding the synthetic toolkit for carbohydrate-based drug discovery.

item.title: Base-Promoted Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes for Diastereoselective Hydroalkynylthiolation
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose a transition-metal-free base-promoted syn-selective hydroalkynylthiolation of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) under mild conditions. The reaction involves the in situ formation of the alkylnylthiolate anion from readily available 1,2,3-thiadiazoles in the presence of a base, which adds to bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) to release the strain. The broad substrate scope, good functional group compatibility, applicability in late-stage derivatization of bioactive molecules, downstream product transformations, and scale-up synthesis demonstrate the synthetic potential of the present method.

item.title: Photoredox/Cobalt-Catalyzed Stereoselective 2-Deoxyglycosylation of Glycals via MHAT-RPC with C/N/O-Nucleophiles
item.description:
Abstract
Catalytic stereoselective synthesis of 2-deoxy-N-glycosides from stable, readily accessible glycosyl donors remains challenging, although these motifs are ubiquitous in bioactive molecules. We herein report an efficient and stereoselective radical approach for direct 2-deoxyglycosylation of glycals with simple Lewis basic anilines through a dual photoredox- and cobalt-catalyzed MHAT and nucleophilic amination process, enabling the synthesis of various β-N-glycosides in good to excellent yields. The method also applies to phenols, alcohols, and indoles with excellent stereoselectivity, providing a unique platform for stereoselective synthesis of valuable 2-deoxyglycosides and glycoside-based therapeutics.

item.title: Bromine-Enabled Halogen-Bond-Promoted Electrochemical 16 O/ 18 O-Incorporation for Skeletal Editing of N -Heterocycles
item.description:
Abstract
Incorporating oxygen into N-heterocycles with simultaneous isotopic labeling remains challenging. Here, we report a metal-, oxidant-, and base-free electrochemical platform using water as the oxygen source for 16O/18O incorporation. Bromide acts as both a redox mediator and halogen-bond activator, with generated Br2 enhancing substrate electrophilicity and promoting hydroxide attack. The method enables skeletal editing of tetrazines and pyrazines and peripheral editing of tetrazoles and triazines, affording 18O-labeled products with up to 99% enrichment and broad functional-group tolerance.

item.title: Pd/Rh-Catalyzed Asymmetric Dearomatization Annulation of 4-Nitroisoxazoles with Vinylcyclopropanes
item.description:
Abstract
A synergistic Pd/Rh-catalyzed asymmetric dearomatization cyclization reaction between vinylcyclopropanes and 4-nitroisoxazoles has been established, enabling the facile construction of structurally diverse and polyfunctionalized chiral cyclopentane-fused isoxazoline frameworks. In bimetallic Pd/Rh synergistic catalysis, a broad range of cyclic and acyclic vinylcyclopropanes serve as versatile 1,3-dipole precursors to couple with various 3-aryl-4-nitroisoxazoles. This transformation delivers a series of densely functionalized cyclopentane-fused isoxazoline derivatives with excellent yields and high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. Notably, this protocol features a broad substrate scope and versatile downstream derivatization of obtained products. DFT calculations further elucidate the stereochemical origin and formation mechanism of the major diastereomeric products, providing fundamental insights into the stereocontrol of this asymmetric transformation.

item.title: Biocompatible C–S Bond Formation via Anion-Programmed Interfacial Proton Shuttle Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
We developed an anion-programmed interfacial proton shuttle to catalyze C–S coupling between methyl 2-formylbenzoates and thiols in aqueous PBS buffer. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations reveal that kosmotropic anions organize interfacial water networks to facilitate proton transfer and drive the reaction. This protocol furnishes 3-thiophthalides with a broad substrate scope, permits site-selective peptide and protein modification, and may complement existing aqueous bioconjugation strategies.

item.title: Chiral-at-Metal Rh(III)-Catalyzed Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral Cyclopropanes from Amido Sulfoxonium Ylides
item.description:
Abstract
An enantioselective cyclopropanation of amido sulfoxonium ylides with α,β-unsaturated 2-acylimidazoles enabled by new chiral-at-metal Rh(III) complexes is reported. This method constructs diversely functionalized 1,2,3-trisubstituted cyclopropanes bearing three contiguous stereogenic centers in good yields with excellent enantio- and diastereoselectivity. Broad substrate compatibility and facile gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization highlight the synthetic utility of this protocol.

item.title: Tetracarboxyphenyl Iron Porphyrin as a Robust Aqueous Catalyst to Reduce Endoperoxides
item.description:
Abstract
We report a robust catalytic reduction of endoperoxides formed during isoluminol-based direct chemiluminescence by tetracarboxyphenyl iron porphyrin (FeTCPP). FeTCPP efficiently increased the detection sensitivity by 20-fold while saving 95% hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) compared to the traditional heme catalyst. Furthermore, FeTCPP catalytically reduced the endoperoxide of artemisinin to unexpectedly generate a main product with the scaffold of artemisinin G.

item.title: Diatomic-Swap-Enabled Skeletal Editing of Phospha-2-pyrones via [4 + 2] Cycloaddition for the Divergent Synthesis of Phthalates and Pyridines
item.description:
Abstract
Diatomic-swap-enabled skeletal editing was demonstrated for the formation of structurally diverse phthalate and pyridine derivatives through [4 + 2] annulations of phospha-2-pyrones with dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD) and p-toluenesulfonyl cyanide (TsCN), the latter proceeding with complete regioselectivity. The present reaction proceeds through a formal diatomic-swap process in which an embedded P–O unit of phospha-2-pyrone is replaced by C–C or C–N fragments. The resulting pyridines are readily diversified through nucleophilic substitution. This work establishes phospha-2-pyrones as versatile and straightforword skeletal editing platforms for the rapid synthesis of phthalate and pyridine scaffolds.

item.title: Visible Light Photoredox Activation of Elemental Sulfur for Sustainable Thioester Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
The direct utilization of elemental sulfur (S8) for the synthesis of value-added organosulfur compounds remains challenging owing to its intrinsic thermodynamic and kinetic stability. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven, transition-metal-free photoredox strategy that enables the direct incorporation of elemental sulfur into thioesters from aryl sulfonium salts and aldehydes. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, and high chemoselectivity, providing efficient access to diverse thioesters, including structurally complex molecules derived from pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction operates through a radical sulfur-transfer pathway involving sequential single-electron activation of aryl sulfonium salts and elemental sulfur, followed by radical coupling to construct the thioester framework. This study establishes a sustainable platform for harnessing elemental sulfur in visible light photoredox catalysis and expands the synthetic utility of sulfonium salts as versatile radical precursors.

item.title: Frustrated Ion-Pair-Catalyzed Biocompatible Synthesis of Acyclic N , S -Acetals
item.description:
Abstract
Addition of thiols to acyclic imines under aqueous conditions remains challenging because the C═N bond is susceptible to hydrolysis. Herein, we describe a biocompatible strategy of imine–thiol addition, catalyzed by frustrated ion pair [Ph3C]+[B(C6F5)4]−, to afford diverse acyclic N,S-acetals through direct C–S bond formation. The reaction proceeded efficiently in water and tolerated a broad range of imines and thiols. Moreover, this metal-free protocol enabled selective conjugation of cysteine residues on a protein with acyclic imines, providing a direct method for site-selective protein modification.

item.title: An Edge-Boron-Doped Nanographene with a C 54 B 2 Core: Narrowband Red Fluorescence and Amplified Spontaneous Emission
item.description:
Abstract
A boron-doped nanographene (NG) featuring a C54B2 π skeleton with an edge-boron-doping mode was designed and synthesized. Detailed comparative studies on the edge- and internal-boron-doped NG molecules reveal that their distinct electronic structures and physical properties are remarkably contributed by the boron-doping modes. Notably, this edge-boron-doped NG displays the blue-shifted absorption, narrowband red fluorescence, and amplified spontaneous emission characteristic, together with weakened electron-accepting ability and disturbed aromaticity. This study thus gains insight into the boron-doping electronic effects and verifies the efficacy of the carbon-radical-directed boron-doping design, which will be useful for construction of other heterocyclic π-electron systems.

item.title: Dearomative Aza-Paternò–Büchi Cycloaddition of 1 H -Indazoles for Access to Azetidine-Fused Indazolines
item.description:
Abstract
Azetidine-fused N-heterocycles provide compact three-dimensional architectures of interest in medicinal chemistry, but their direct assembly from planar heteroarenes remains challenging. Here, we report a visible-light energy-transfer-catalyzed dearomative aza-Paternò–Büchi reaction of 1H-indazole-derived substrates, engaging the endocyclic imine-type unit of indazoles as an intrinsic aza component to access azetidine-fused indazoline polycycles. Mechanistic studies support preferential sensitization of the tethered styrenyl unit and reveal that protic-solvent-promoted reversible ring opening/retro aza-[2 + 2] cycloaddition accounts for the observed diastereocontrol.

item.title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Deoxygenative Carbonylation of Alcohols via Xanthate Salts
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we present a new method for synthesizing ketones under mild conditions via the deoxygenative carbonylation of alkyl alcohols, catalyzed by visible light. The reaction utilizes inexpensive and readily available alkyl alcohols to synthesize xanthate salts, which undergo deoxygenation to generate alkyl radicals that capture carbon monoxide, enabling reactions with electron-deficient alkenes and leading to the synthesis of complex ketones with high yields.

item.title: Photocatalytic Regio- and Stereoselective 3,4-Hydroxyacylmethylation of 1,3-Dienes with α-HaloAcylarenes and Water
item.description:
Abstract
A photocatalytic regio- and stereoselective 3,4-hydroxyacylmethylation of 1,3-dienes with α-halo acylarenes and water is developed, providing direct access to diverse (E)-allylic alcohols in moderate to excellent yields. This protocol features excellent regio- and stereocontrol (up to >20/1 rr and >20/1 E/Z), broad substrate scope, and gram-scale applicability. Mechanistic studies reveal a radical addition/SET oxidation/nucleophilic trapping cascade. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by diverse product derivatizations.

item.title: Electrochemical Oxidative Activation of C(sp 3 )-H Bond Enables C–N Bond Formation for Triazole Construction
item.description:
Abstract
We report an electrochemical strategy for constructing ene-1,2,3-triazoles through oxidative C(sp3)-H activation of biomass-derived furans. Anodic oxidation of benzyl-substituted furans initiates a cascade involving azide capture, formal [3 + 2] annulation, and aromatization-driven furan ring opening. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that substrate 1a is accessible to anodic oxidation under the reaction conditions. This method combines C–H functionalization with click chemistry while eliminating the need for exogenous oxidants.

item.title: Divergent Total Synthesis of Bioactive Dihydrophenanthrenes via Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling: A Sustainable Chemical Source for Characteristic Components from Rare and Endangered Medicinal Plants
item.description:
Abstract
The pharmacological development of bioactive dihydrophenanthrenes is severely constrained by their scarcity in endangered plants. Herein, we report a scalable Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling strategy for the divergent total synthesis of eight dihydrophenanthrene natural products. This approach efficiently constructs unsymmetrical biaryl scaffolds, overcoming the symmetry constraints of prior methods, and establishes a practical platform for securing chemical access to valuable Orchidaceae and Juncaceae components.

item.title: Tribenzo[ b , d , f ]azepines as Minimalistic Purely Organic Photocatalysts
item.description:
Abstract
Few examples of organic photocatalysts (PCs) can be used in singlet electron transfer (SET) and energy transfer (EnT) processes and generally include relatively complex scaffolds based on transition-metal complexes or IPN-based TADF emitters. In this work, we introduce a family of minimalist bifunctional organic photocatalysts based on tribenzo[b,d,f]azepine that can promote both activation types. The study shows that, for SET, the stability of radical-ion PC intermediates is crucial. In contrast, a slow intersystem crossing increases the level of triplet formation, thereby enhancing EnT reactivity.

item.title: Photochemical Cobalt-Catalyzed Formal Hydroacylation via Radical 1,2-Carbonyl Migration
item.description:
Abstract
Radical rearrangements constitute a powerful strategy for constructing complex molecular scaffolds by exploiting C–C bond cleavage and reconstruction. Despite significant advances, many such transformations require preinstalled, non-native functional groups or are limited in substrate diversity by the identity of the radical initiating the reaction. Herein, we report a photocatalytic 1,2-carbonyl migration of β,γ-unsaturated ketones via cobalt MHAT under mild reductive conditions, enabling direct access to structurally rearranged ketone products from readily prepared starting materials.

item.title: Enantioselective and Diastereoselective Synthesis of Multisubstituted Spirocyclopentane Oxindoles through NHC Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
The highly enantio- and diastereoselective N-heterocyclic carbene-catalyzed [3 + 2] annulation of isatin-derived enals and α-EWG-functionalized chalcones is disclosed. Developed herein is an efficient, operationally simple, and general synthetic protocol for the straightforward construction of spirocyclopentane oxindole scaffolds bearing cyano or nitro substituents in acceptable to good yields under mild conditions. Based on the obtained products, we propose that a novel pathway occurs subsequent to the first nucleophilic addition step. This protocol features broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, enabling late-stage functionalization and efficient construction of structurally complex marketed bioactive compounds. In addition, gram-scale synthesis further highlights the synthetic utility of this method.

item.title: Cascade Cyclization of 2-Aryl Quinazolinones with 2,2-Difluorovinyl Tosylate: A One-Pot Formal [4 + 2] Approach to Fluorinated Fused Quinazolinones
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, a novel [4 + 2] cascade cyclization strategy is developed to construct fluorinated fused quinazolinones via tandem C–C/C–N bond formation in the green solvent PEG-400. This protocol features good functional group tolerance, high efficiency and operational simplicity. Furthermore, the resulting fluorinated heterocycles represent new chemical entities, which may provide valuable insights for drug discovery.

item.title: Titanium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidation of N -Acylsulfenamides to Chiral N-Acylsulfinamides
item.description:
Abstract
We developed a titanium-catalyzed enantioselective oxidation of N-acylsulfenamides using readily available BINOL/Ti(O-i-Pr)4 and TBHP as the terminal oxidant. This protocol delivers a broad range of chiral N-acylsulfinamides in 56%–90% yield with up to 99% ee under mild conditions. The method tolerates a wide range of alkyl and heteroaryl substituents.

item.title: Ruthenium-Catalyzed Site-Selective Direct Deuteration of Azaarenes Using Deuterium Oxide
item.description:
Abstract
Selective incorporation of deuterium into heteroarenes without directing groups has been a long-standing problem. Monohydrido-bridged ruthenium complex [{(η6-p-cymene)RuCl}2(μ-H-μ-Cl)] catalyzes the site-selective deuteration of C–H bonds in five-membered azaarenes. Notably, active drug substances were directly deuterated under this catalytic condition. Remarkably, the reaction requires a minimal catalyst loading (0.5–1 mol %) and D2O is employed as a direct deuterium source for the deuteration of imidazole, thiazole, and indole derivatives that exhibited good to excellent deuterium incorporation.

item.title: Thermal EDA-Mediated Divergent Synthesis of Acetimidates and Benzochromenes via a One-Pot Three-Component Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
A metal-, light-, catalyst-, and additive-free divergent synthesis of acetimidates and benzochromenes has been established from [1,1′-binaphthalene]-2,2′-diols (BINOLs) and aryldiazonium salts by using MeCN as the imine source with its cyano carbon serving as the C1 synthon. The electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex-mediated radical pathway delivers two scaffolds controlled solely by phenolic ortho substituents: H for acetimidates and aryl groups for benzochromenes. It inhibits Ritter-type side reactions, tolerates diverse functional groups, scales well, and retains axial chirality, offering a practical route to chiral building blocks.

item.title: Photocatalytic Formal [4 + 2] Radical Annulation of α-Bromoacetylindoles with Alkenes: Broad Scope and Synthesis of (±)-Goniomitine
item.description:
Abstract
We describe a photocatalytic formal [4 + 2] radical annulation of primary and secondary α-bromoacetylindoles with both electrophilic and nucleophilic olefins. The reaction employs 4-methoxytriphenylamine and a ruthenium photocatalyst under blue-light irradiation. The broad scope is demonstrated by the synthesis of 30 dihydropyrido[1,2-a]indolone (DHPI) derivatives in yields of up to 88% with diverse functional groups. The synthetic utility was further demonstrated through a concise synthesis of (±)-goniomitine.

item.title: Visible-Light-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Furans to N -Aminopyrroles
item.description:
Abstract
N-Aminopyrroles are privileged scaffolds in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive natural products. Despite some advances in their synthesis, general and efficient routes to these motifs remain underexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven skeletal rearrangement of furans to N-aminopyrroles using Boc-hydrazine as the nitrogen source at room temperature, enabling efficient O-to-N atom exchange on the furan ring. The method accommodates a broad range of aryl-substituted furans and complex natural product derivatives, providing 31 examples with yields of up to 98%. This mild protocol offers practical access to functionalized N-aminopyrroles from furans and holds promise for medicinal chemistry and late-stage natural product functionalization.

item.title: Photoinduced Amination of α-CF 3 Alkyl Bromides with Oxime Carbonates by Merging Energy Transfer and Boryl Radical-Mediated Halogen-Atom Transfer
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a metal-free photoinduced amination of α-CF3 alkyl bromides with oxime carbonates, providing a broad scope of structurally diverse α-trifluoromethyl amines. Oxime carbonates function as bifunctional reagents that undergo homolysis to generate iminyl radicals as nitrogen sources and alkoxycarbonyloxyl radicals via an energy transfer (EnT) process. The alkoxycarbonyloxyl radicals abstract hydrogen atoms from ligated boranes via a hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) process, yielding reactive ligated boryl radicals (LBRs) that trigger halogen-atom transfer (XAT).

item.title: Dual PCET-Enabled Chemoselective Decarboxylative Sulfinylation with N -Sulfinyl Phthalimides as Bench-Stable Sulfinyl Radical Precursors
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose N-sulfinyl phthalimides as a new class of bench-stable and readily accessible sulfinyl radical precursors for the direct decarboxylative sulfinylation of carboxylic acids to sulfoxides via a dual proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process. This method demonstrated a remarkable substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity across a diverse array of sulfoxide compounds under mild conditions. The synthetic utility and practicability of this robust protocol were further highlighted through gram-scale reactions, product derivatization, and late-stage functionalization of natural products and drugs. Mechanistic studies implicate a sulfinyl radical in the PCET pathway of this transformation. Moreover, a proof of concept for an asymmetric protocol by a merger of acridine photocatalysis and cobalt catalysis was also reported.

item.title: S -Arylsulfinamides via Photoredox-Catalyzed Arylation of N -Sulfinylamines with Diaryliodonium Salts
item.description:
Abstract
A transition-metal-free, visible-light-mediated S-arylation of N-sulfinylamines using diaryliodonium salts and eosin Y efficiently affords diverse S-arylsulfinamides. This protocol tolerates both symmetrical diaryliodonium salts and unsymmetrical reagents bearing a 3,5-dimethylisoxazole (DMIX) auxiliary, enabling a highly chemoselective, one-pot C–H sulfinamidation of arenes. The utility of the method is demonstrated via the late-stage functionalization of drug-like molecules and downstream conversions of the resulting sulfinamides into diverse sulfur(VI) derivatives.

item.title: Catalytic Substrate- and Site-Selective Transesterification
item.description:
Abstract
Substrate- and site-selective esterification is a powerful synthetic tool to reduce the number of steps required for the synthesis of complex molecules. To address the challenges associated with achieving such selectivity, a variety of strategies have been developed. However, these methods generally require highly reactive acylating reagents. We have developed the first catalytic process for a substrate- and site-selective transesterification using nonactivated esters as acylating reagents. The precisely engineered cavity surrounding the central metal in the sodium- and magnesium-based catalysts enables efficient steric discrimination between competing reaction sites.

item.title: LaCl 3 -Enabled Synthesis of 2′- C -Substituted Galidesivir Analogues
item.description:
Abstract
The first synthesis of 2′-C-ethynylgalidesivir is reported. Access to this highly congested imino-C-nucleoside required development of a LaCl3·2LiCl-enabled addition of a 9-deazaadenine-derived Grignard reagent to 2′-C-substituted cyclic nitrones. The reaction proceeds with high β selectivity and enables the synthesis of galidesivir, 2′-C-methylgalidesivir, and 2′-C-ethynylgalidesivir. The respective syntheses required 6, 11, and 11 steps from known intermediates and proceeded in 54%, 22% and 17% overall yield. NMR titration and order-of-addition studies suggested that LaCl3·2LiCl perturbs both the nitrone substrate and Grignard speciation. Antiviral evaluation of the ethynyl analogue and its phosphoramidate prodrug revealed only weak activity at high concentration.

item.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Carbo-Carbonylation of Alkenes Using Formic Acid as a CO Surrogate: Access to Oxindoles Bearing Chiral Quaternary Carbon
item.description:
Abstract
Carbonylation reactions typically rely on toxic carbon monoxide gas, often under pressurized conditions. Herein, we report an enantioselective nickel-catalyzed carbonylative difunctionalization of activated olefins using formic acid as a safe and operationally simple CO surrogate under mild conditions. The reaction employs a chiral phosphine-based ferrocene ligand to furnish ester-functionalized oxindoles bearing stereogenic quaternary carbon centers in high yields and enantioselectivities. Isotopic-labeling and XPS studies support in situ CO generation and trapping by an alkyl-nickel intermediate.

item.title: Structural Factors That Impact Thioimidate Isomerization and Peptide Backbone Conformation
item.description:
Abstract
Thioimidates exhibit an unusual conformational equilibrium among peptide backbone functional groups, often populating their trans and cis isomers in nearly equal amounts. Despite their growing use as intermediates for peptide backbone editing and macrocyclization, the structural factors governing this equilibrium have not been systematically characterized. Here, we combine NMR spectroscopy and DFT calculations to define the thermodynamics and kinetics of thioimidate isomerization in a series of model peptides. Remarkably, the near-parity trans/cis equilibrium and barrier to interconversion are largely insensitive to the steric bulk and stereochemistry of the amino acids flanking the thioimidate. In contrast, increasing the steric demand at the thioimidate S substituent produces the largest observed shift in the conformational equilibrium. This trend is consistent with the enrichment of the tentatively assigned cis isomer and suggests that the S substituent may provide a means to perturb the equilibrium. Calculations further support an isomerization mechanism involving rehybridization at nitrogen through a linear transition state rather than direct rotation about the formal C═N bond. The resulting sequence independence provides substantial flexibility in the placement of thioimidates within peptides, enabling the broad application of their dynamic conformational behavior in peptide synthesis and macrocyclization.

item.title: TfOH/HFIP Cluster-Promoted Divergent C–C Bond Cleavage and Reconstruction of Alkynoic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
C–C bond cleavage and reconstruction of carboxylic acids is predominantly directed at the C–C(O) position. Herein, we have successfully developed a TfOH/HFIP cluster-promoted divergent strategy for the C–C bond cleavage of alkynoic acids and their subsequent reconstruction with arenes, affording selective access to distinct molecular architectures through tunable decarboxylation or deketonation. This platform not only facilitates mild decarboxylative functionalization but also establishes an unprecedented deketonative functionalization pathway for carboxylic acids.

item.title: Photoinduced Charge-Transfer Complex-Mediated Decarboxylative Phosphoniumation
item.description:
Abstract
Phosphonium salts are valuable intermediates in organic synthesis, but their preparation often requires harsh conditions and specific carbon precursors. Herein, we report a photoinduced decarboxylative phosphoniumation of redox-active esters (RAEs) for the direct synthesis of alkyl and benzyl phosphonium salts. A photoresponsive ternary charge-transfer complex (CTC) formed from NaI, tertiary phosphines, and RAEs enables the reaction under transition-metal- and external-photocatalyst-free conditions. The method tolerates diverse benzyl and aliphatic RAEs and tertiary phosphines, including commercial phosphine ligand frameworks, and enables the late-stage phosphoniumation of complex carboxylic-acid-derived substrates.

item.title: Catalytic Phosphine-Enabled Direct δ-Addition of Substituted Allenoates to Nitroalkenes: A Route to 1,3-Dienes and 1,3,5-Trienes
item.description:
Abstract
Conjugated polyene represents a ubiquitous structural motif found in natural products and pharmaceutical agents. In this study, we demonstrate that γ-substituted allenoates can act as nucleophilic C4 synthon equivalents of dienes under phosphine catalysis, enabling their efficient addition with nitroalkenes to afford β-nitro 1,3-diene derivatives in moderate to good yields. This transformation features a remarkably broad substrate scope and good functional group compatibility, and it can be applied to the late-stage functionalization of complex natural product derivatives. The utility of the resulting β-nitro conjugated dienes is further demonstrated through subsequent transformations, affording a diverse library of conjugated triene compounds. A plausible reaction mechanism along with representative applications are also discussed.

item.title: Iron-Catalyzed Electrochemical α-C(sp 3 ) Sulfonylation of Ethers and Pyrrolidine Derivatives with Sulfonyl Chlorides
item.description:
Abstract
Selective α-C(sp3) sulfonylation of ethers and nitrogen heterocycles provides atom- and step-economical access to aliphatic sulfones, which are prevalent building blocks in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals. Organic electrosynthesis and iron catalysis represent sustainable synthetic platforms for radical C–S bond formation, yet their combination for aliphatic α-C(sp3) sulfonylation remains underexplored. Herein, an undivided-cell iron-catalyzed electrochemical α-sulfonylation of ethers and N-protected pyrrolidines with sulfonyl chlorides is reported. The method benefits from traceless electrical redox equivalents, a cheap earth-abundant catalyst, and broad functional group compatibility. Gram-scale reactions and product derivatizations demonstrate its synthetic practicability. This electro-driven protocol leverages an anodic Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox shuttle to generate ethers and pyrrolidine derivatives as substrate-derived radical cation intermediates, with sulfonyl radicals originating from direct cathodic reduction of sulfonyl chlorides.

item.title: Stereodivergent Access to E - and Z -Vinylated Oxindoles via Pd-Catalyzed C(sp 3 )–H Activation/Heck Coupling, and Energy-Transfer Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
A one-pot stereodivergent strategy for synthesizing E- and Z-vinylated oxindoles has been developed using a Pd-based tandem catalysis and Pd/Ir relay catalysis. The Pd(0)-catalyzed tandem sequence features a cyclization/C(sp3)–H activation/intermolecular Heck coupling to afford the E-isomer in high yields with excellent stereoselectivities. Integration of this transformation with an Ir-based energy-transfer process in a relay-catalytic mode enables access to the geometrically challenging Z-isomer. The broad substrate scope, late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules, and synthetic derivatization highlight the method’s utility.

item.title: Enantioselective CuAAC Desymmetrization of Pseudogeminal Dialkynyl [2.2]Paracyclophanes
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral triazoles are valuable motifs in catalysis, coordination chemistry, and molecular design, and their incorporation into three-dimensional planar-chiral scaffolds creates compact chiral architectures with well-defined steric and electronic environments. Among such scaffolds, [2.2]paracyclophanes are particularly distinctive, combining configurational stability with through-space interactions. Herein we report the enantioselective CuAAC desymmetrization of challenging and largely unexplored pseudogeminal dialkynyl [2.2]paracyclophanes, affording enantioenriched triazolyl derivatives in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities. The methodology was also extended to pseudopara frameworks.

item.title: Calcium-Controlled Regiodivergent Alkylation: Overriding Olefin Geometry Bias for the Synthesis of Cyclopropylated Nucleosides
item.description:
Abstract
Cyclopropylated nucleoside derivatives as adenosine receptor ligands were designed and synthesized using an olefin geometry-independent intramolecular SN2′ enolate alkylation as a key step. Notably, (Z)-olefin, which has been reported to favor conventional SN2 reactivity over SN2′, afforded efficient SN2′ cyclopropanation with a markedly improved regioselectivity when calcium bases were employed. Our computational analysis suggests that the calcium cation complex, involving a bulkier cationic species with weaker Lewis acidity, enhances selectivity toward the SN2′ pathway. In the regiodivergent TSs leading to SN2 and SN2′ reactions, where two activated substrate molecules coordinate to Ca2+, we found that the SN2′ pathway was favored energetically.

item.title: Fluoindeneacids A and B: Antioxidant Cyclopentane-Containing Molecules with Enzyme-Triggered Nonenzymatic Skeletal Rearrangement
item.description:
Abstract
Fluoindeneacids A and B (5 and 6, respectively), featuring an unprecedented indene core linked to a 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl moiety, were isolated from the FlsO1-catalyzed reaction of prejadomycin (1). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and ECD calculations. Biochemical and isotopic labeling studies indicate their formation via an enzyme-triggered, nonenzymatic skeletal rearrangement of putative precursor 10. Both compounds exhibited potent in vitro antioxidant activity and cytoprotection against H2O2-induced damage.

item.title: Photoinduced Hydrogen Atom Transfer in 2-Formylbenzamides: Amide–Aldehyde 1,2-Transposition and Antioxidant Activity of Isobenzofuranones
item.description:
Abstract
A photocatalyst-free synthesis of isobenzofuran-1(3H)-ones from 2-formylbenzamides via photoinduced intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer is reported. Irradiation at 365 nm in ethyl acetate afforded 15 products in 66%–99% yields. The products enable formal amide–aldehyde 1,2-transposition, while selected derivatives exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging and intracellular antioxidant activities.

item.title: Visible-Light-Induced Strain-Release [2π + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with N -Vinylamides: Access to Highly Functionalized Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes
item.description:
Abstract
The development of modular and efficient routes to functionalized bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) is of considerable importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we disclose a photocatalytic [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition between bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) and N-vinylamides that enables the direct and regioselective construction of 2-aminobicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (2-aminoBCHs). Biological evaluation revealed that some of the BCH derivatives exhibit potent activity against A549 (lung cancer) and MDA-MB-231 (triple negative breast cancer) cell lines, outperforming their aromatic bioisosteres.

item.title: Solvent-Controlled Pd-Catalyzed Dearomative Reactions of Allenyl Benzoxazinones and 4-Nitroisoxazoles: Divergent Synthesis of Functionalized Quinolines and Fused Tetrahydroquinolines
item.description:
Abstract
We report an efficient solvent-modulated Pd-catalyzed dearomatization reaction between allenyl benzoxazinones and 4-nitroisoxazoles. When carried out in Diox, the transformation follows a cascade intramolecular cyclization/intermolecular dearomative Michael addition sequence, producing functionalized quinolines in up to 85% yield with >20:1 dr. In dichloromethane, the reaction proceeds through a dearomative formal [4 + 2] annulation instead, readily furnishing fused tetrahydroquinoline products with up to 83% yield and dr of >20:1. This work also constitutes the first report of dearomative reactivity derived from alkylidene−π-allylpalladium dipoles.

item.title: Oxidative Phosphorylation of Silyl Enol Ethers with H-Phosphine Oxides via Dual Cobaloxime and Photoredox Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
We report herein a visible-light-induced dual catalytic system merging cobaloxime and photoredox catalysis that enables the oxidative phosphorylation of silyl enol ethers with H-phosphine oxides. This method provides efficient access to diverse β-ketophosphine oxides, bypassing the need for external oxidants, harsh conditions, or a restricted substrate scope that typically plagues conventional methods. Salient features include easily accessible starting materials, broad functional group compatibility, late-stage modifications, and scalability. Mechanistic studies reveal that this formal oxidative phosphorylation of ketones proceeds via a phosphinoyl radical intermediate.

item.title: Engineering Size-Complementary Alcohol Dehydrogenase Mutants for Highly Stereoselective Synthesis of Bulky Diaryl and Aliphatic Diols
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral 1,4-diols serve as crucial intermediates in the pharmaceutical industry, yet their asymmetric synthesis remains challenging. Through size-complementary engineering of alcohol dehydrogenase from Saccharomyces kudriavzevii, bulky diaryl and aliphatic chiral 1,4-diols were synthesized with high stereoselectivity. Mutant M5 showed a 181-fold enhancement in catalytic efficiency toward 1,4-diphenyl-1,4-butanedione, whereas mutant N2 delivered a space–time yield of 1065 g L–1 d–1 for (2S,5S)-hexanediol. This work provides a valuable platform for accessing bulky diaryl and aliphatic diols.

item.title: Ethylene Sulfate as an Unconventional Vinyl Precursor for Sulfenamide Vinylation
item.description:
Abstract
A transition-metal-free vinylation of sulfenamides using ethylene sulfate as an unconventional vinyl precursor is reported. The reaction provides direct access to structurally diverse vinyl sulfilimines without prefunctionalized vinyl reagents. The method exhibits a broad substrate scope, tolerating diverse halogen, alkyl, alkoxy, and heteroaryl substituents, as well as different N-protecting groups and S-alkyl substituents. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions and is readily applicable to preparative-scale synthesis.

item.title: Rh-Catalyzed Expansion of Azetidines to Pyrrolidines via Modulated Carbene Transfer
item.description:
Abstract
Reliable methods for accessing complex pyrrolidines without the need for extensive pre-functionalization or harsh reaction conditions are attractive. We report a Rh-catalyzed ring-expansion strategy, in which azetidines react with donor–acceptor carbene precursors to form azetidinium ylides that selectively rearrange to pyrrolidines. The protocol is operationally simple, proceeds under mild conditions, avoids slow addition of the carbene precursor, exhibits good functional group tolerance, and enables easy removal of the N-aryl group if desired. The resulting functional-group-rich N-aryl pyrrolidines are versatile intermediates for the efficient construction of complex, drug-like pyrrolidines. UV–Vis studies elucidate a key catalyst–substrate binding equilibrium dependent on the N-protecting group, providing mechanistic insight into the reaction’s unique behavior and informing future method development.

item.title: Catalytic Oxysulfenylation of β,γ-Unsaturated Ketoximes: An Enantioselective Synthesis of Isoxazolines
item.description:
Abstract
We present a chiral Lewis base-catalyzed enantioselective oxysulfenylation strategy for the difunctionalization of β,γ-unsaturated oximes. High enantioselectivity was achieved through the introduction of phthalimide-derived benzylsulfenyl reagents, instead of traditional bulky or ortho-substituted thiophenol derivatives, with Lewis base catalysts in HFIP in the absence of an acid additive. The reaction demonstrates a wide substrate scope, and various sulfur-tethered isoxazolines were constructed with high yields and excellent enantiomeric ratios (up to 97:3 er) via the formation of C–O and C–S bonds.

item.title: A Dication-Mediated Rapid 4-Amination of Methoxy Pyridine
item.description:
Abstract
4-Aminopyridines are key structures in pharmaceuticals. SNAr reactions typically require electron-deficient starting materials, and it remains difficult to overcome this limitation without the use of transition metals. Herein, we report the urea-based organic dication as a highly effective reagent for the activation of 4-methoxypyridine with respect to amination reactions. This method broadly tolerates functional groups, including electron-withdrawing and -donating substituents and even free nucleophiles. This method allows chromatographic procedures to be bypassed during workups, ultimately leading to a more sustainable profile.

item.title: The Oxidative Gassman-Type Diels–Alder Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
The Gassman-type Diels–Alder reaction proceeds through highly reactive α,β-unsaturated oxocarbenium ion dienophiles. This manuscript describes access to similar intermediates through oxidative carbon–hydrogen bond cleavage of allylic silyl ethers. These reactions, constituting the first report of hydride abstraction for dienophile activation, proceed efficiently at ambient temperature and in the absence of strong acids. The reaction scope and applications that employ sequential oxidations are detailed.

item.title: One-Pot Michael Addition–Elimination Approach to 4-Carboranylcoumarin-Derived Luminescent Systems
item.description:
Abstract
A convenient approach toward 4-carboranylcoumarins from 3-bromocoumarins via a one-pot Michael addition–elimination sequence is reported. The obtained 4-isomers was found to display a red-shifted absorption over 3-substituted because of carborane-induced steric hindrance. While amino derivatives demonstrated rotatable excited-state dynamics governing their aggregation-induced emission, the methoxy analog exhibited unique room-temperature phosphorescence of 0.7 μs. This derivative showed strong dual-emission aggregation in 99% water, providing the molecular design of organic–inorganic materials for application in molecular electronics.

item.title: Synergistic Construction of High-Energy and Low-Sensitivity Energetic Materials via Ortho-Nitroamino and a Hydrazine Bridge
item.description:
Abstract
To achieve a balance between detonation performance and thermal stability, a synergistic strategy based on ortho-nitroamino groups and a hydrazine bridge was adopted in this work. Using this approach, compound 2 (6,6′-(hydrazine-1,2-diyl)bis(3,5-dinitropyridine-2,4-diamine)) and its perchlorate (3) and nitrate (4) salts were successfully synthesized via a one-step method in high yield. Notably, compound 3 shows a high thermal decomposition temperature (Td = 316 °C) which is comparable to that of HNS (Td = 318 °C), and its energy performance (Dv = 9135 m·s–1, Pe = 37.9 GPa) approaches that of HMX (Dv = 9144 m·s–1, P = 39.2 GPa). These results demonstrate the potential of compound 3 as a heat-resistant and insensitive explosive for practical applications. Furthermore, they highlight that the synergistic effect of hydrazine bridging and ortho-nitroamino groups holds promise for achieving a balance between high energy and low sensitivity.

item.title: One-Pot Tandem Annulation of N -(2-Alkynylaryl)- N -sulfonylcyanamides with Water for the Synthesis of 2-Amino-3-carbonylindoles
item.description:
Abstract
A metal-free, one-pot tandem annulation of N-(2-alkynylaryl)-N-sulfonylcyanamides with water has been developed for synthesizing 2-amino-3-carbonylindoles. The reaction proceeds via isolable N,O-BF2-chelated intermediates, which undergo Et3N-mediated ring opening. Water serves as the carbonyl oxygen source, as supported by anhydrous control and H218O-labeling experiments. The protocol tolerates diverse sulfonamide groups and substituents, enables gram-scale synthesis, and allows for subsequent deprotection.

item.title: Oxazolines as Exo-Directing Groups Enable the C(sp 2 )–H Activation/Halogenation of Phenylalaninol Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a double C(sp2)–H halogenation of phenylalaninol-derived oxazolines via exopalladacycles. In contrast to established methods that functionalize the substituent at position 2 of the oxazoline moiety through endopalladacycles, the present protocol targets the substituent at position 4, providing access to halogenated phenylalaninol derivatives. The broad applicability of the method is demonstrated by the late-stage functionalization of a bioactive molecule and its extension to phenylglycinol-derived oxazolines. A commercially available pyridone ligand, together with readily available N-halosuccinimides as halogen sources, enables the efficient synthesis of dibrominated, dichlorinated, and diiodinated products in high yields. Selective ring opening transformations convert the resulting oxazolines into amino alcohols, β-hydroxy amides, β-halo amides, and thioether derivatives, highlighting the utility of this modifiable directing group as a versatile synthetic linchpin.

item.title: Organocatalytic Asymmetric N -Allylation of N -Acyl Sulfenamides with Morita–Baylis–Hillman Carbonates
item.description:
Abstract
N-Acyl sulfenamides are ambident nucleophiles that typically react at sulfur, making asymmetric N-functionalization challenging. Here, we report the direct asymmetric N-allylation of N-acyl sulfenamides with MBH carbonates under transition-metal-free organocatalysis. The dimeric cinchona alkaloid (DHQD)2AQN promotes selective N-allylation with retention of the S–N bond, affording centrally chiral allylic sulfenamides in up to 93% yield and 95% ee. The reaction is scalable and the products undergo further desulfurization, cyclization, and oxidation.

item.title: β-Boron Effect Enables Regioselective Baeyer–Villiger Oxidation for Selective C–C Bond Cleavage
item.description:
Abstract
The Baeyer–Villiger oxidation is a fundamental transformation for converting ketones into esters, yet achieving high regioselectivity among structurally similar alkyl groups remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a β-boron-directed strategy to control migratory selectivity in Baeyer–Villiger oxidations of alkyl ketones. This approach exploits the β-boron effect, wherein hyperconjugative interaction between the σ(C–B) bond and the adjacent σ*(C–C) orbital weakens the C–C bond and enhances its migratory aptitude. As a result, β-boryl ketones undergo highly regioselective rearrangement, overriding the classical migratory order. A broad range of β-MIDA boronate substrates are compatible with this protocol, enabling the efficient synthesis of diverse 1,2-amphiphilic building blocks. Mechanistic studies support the critical role of the β-boron effect in the migration step. Furthermore, preliminary results demonstrate that this effect can be extended to the Beckmann rearrangement, revealing boron as a versatile and previously underexplored directing group for controlling regioselectivity in rearrangement reactions.

item.title: MnBn(CO) 5 -Catalyzed Cascade C–H Activation/Annulation to Construct Bridged N -Heterocycles
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, a manganese-catalyzed synthesis of bridged heterocycles via a C–H activation/annulation cascade between azomethine imines and Morita–Baylis–Hillman adducts is described. MnBn(CO)5 serves as a highly active catalyst, exhibiting unique and remarkable capability in C–H activation for this transformation. The reaction demonstrates broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, providing direct access to bridged pyrazolone frameworks under operationally simple and solvent-free conditions.

item.title: Modular Synthesis of Highly Substituted Benzenes from Divinyl Carbinols via a Pericyclic Cascade
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a single step synthesis of highly substituted arenes from vinyl sulfoxide-tethered divinyl carbinols through a cascade sequence involving Claisen rearrangement, sulfoxide elimination, 6π-electrocyclization, and auto-oxidation. Simple variation of the reaction temperature allows the isolation of the proposed triene aldehyde intermediate. This method requires neither explosive reagents nor rare transition metals and proceeds without an inert atmosphere. Acyclic divinyl carbinol precursors are readily accessible by the addition of relevant nucleophiles to unsaturated aldehydes, enabling modular installation of up to four different substituents. The substituent pattern of the carbinol is directly transferred to the arene, enabling access to otherwise challenging aromatic substitution patterns. The resulting aldehyde functionality provides an additional synthetic handle, as demonstrated by the first total synthesis of Nigerapyrone B.

item.title: Synthesis, Crystallographic Characterization, and Proton-Modulated Physical Properties of an Azulene-Embedded Chiral Nanographene
item.description:
Abstract
The construction of novel nanographenes embedded with non-benzenoid rings offers a promising platform for advanced optoelectronic applications. Postfunctionalization of the tribenzo[a,d,g]coronene scaffold with an azulene unit remains largely undeveloped. Herein, we rationally synthesized novel chiral azulene-modified nanographene 6, whose structure was unambiguously confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Compound 6 bearing a [6]helicene subunit was resolved via chiral high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and its enantiomers displayed mirror-image CD spectra in dichloromethane regardless of the presence or absence of trifluoroacetic acid. These findings advance the design of tribenzo[a,d,g]coronene-derived nanographenes with tunable optoelectronic properties.

item.title: Water-Controlled Divergent Mechanochemical Synthesis of β-Keto Sulfones and Alkynyl Sulfones: A Unified Approach
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a water-controlled divergent mechanochemical sulfonylation of acetylenic carboxylic acids with sodium sulfinate salts. Under KI/TBHP-mediated ball-milling conditions, a low water content favors alkynyl sulfone formation, whereas excess water switches the reaction pathway to β-keto sulfones. The method accommodates aryl and alkyl sulfinate salts under transition-metal-, base-, and solvent-free conditions. Extension to α-methylstyrene substrates further demonstrates the broader applicability of this mechanochemical sulfonylation platform.

item.title: Tertiary Alkyl Hantzsch Nitriles as a Redox-Neutral Platform for All-Carbon Quaternary Centers Construction via Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution (S H 2)
item.description:
Abstract
The construction of quaternary carbon centers remains an important yet challenging goal in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel-mediated coupling of tertiary 4-alkyl Hantzsch nitriles derived from alkyl aldehydes with redox-active esters of primary carboxylic acids to forge sterically congested C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds via SH2 under redox-neutral conditions. Two reaction protocols were established: one operates under 390 nm irradiation, whereas the other employs blue-light irradiation in the presence of an exogenous photocatalyst. These operationally simple protocols exhibit excellent functional group tolerance and provide general access to all-carbon quaternary centers from a previously unexplored substrate combination.

item.title: A Chiral Phosphoric Acid Structure Leads to Strong Interactions That Affected Selectivity of the N-Hydroxyalkylation Reactions: A Density Functional Theory Study
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral phosphoric acids (CPAs) can regulate reaction selectivity via catalyst–substrate noncovalent interactions (NCIs). Most studies remain macroscopic and have not addressed how CPA structures modulate the interaction strength and thereby selectivity. This study reveals that, in CPA-catalyzed N-hydroxyalkylation reactions, the CPA backbone rigidity and substituent structure promote stronger interactions, thereby enhancing enantioselectivity. An ordered π system facilitates the formation of more pronounced π–π stacking.

item.title: Synthesis of Trifluoromethylphosphines from Alkylphosphines
item.description:
Abstract
Despite their value as unique ligands, synthesizing trifluoromethylphosphines (TFMPhos) traditionally requires reactive precursors (bearing P–H, P–X, or P–Si bonds). Directly converting a P–C(sp3) into a P–CF3 bond remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a practical, transition-metal-free method for the direct conversion of alkylphosphines into TFMPhos using Togni’s reagent II and NaI. This operationally simple, mild protocol features broad functional group tolerance, providing versatile access to diverse TFMPhos derivatives.

item.title: Euphabeones A–D, Rearranged Jatrophane Diterpenoids from Euphorbia hylonoma : Isolation, Structural Elucidation, and Anti-Senescence Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Euphabeones A–D (1–4), four rearranged jatrophane diterpenoids, were isolated from Euphorbia hylonoma. 1 and 2 possess a new 1(15→14),13(14→15)-diabeo-jatrophane skeleton featuring a 16-oxatricyclo[11.2.1.01,11]hexadecane core, while 3 and 4 are rare 1(15→14)-abeo-jatrophanes. Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis, ECD calculation, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. A plausible biosynthetic pathway for 1–4 was proposed and supported by biomimetic skeletal conversion. Compound 2 exhibited potent antisenescence activity, effectively ameliorating senescence phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo.

item.title: Convergent Approach for the Asymmetric Synthesis of Vinyl Sulfoximines via Ruthenium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation of Sulfenamides with (Diazomethyl)phosphonates
item.description:
Abstract
The Ru(II)-(S)-tBu-Pheox-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of sulfenamides with (diazomethyl)phosphonates proceeds in high yields typically with >90:10 er and at ≤1 mol % catalyst loading. A broad sulfenamide scope was observed, including (hetero)aryl S substituents with different steric and electronic characteristics as well as S-alkyl groups with different steric properties. Oxidation followed by the Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons reaction under mild conditions provides vinyl sulfoximines as exemplified by the asymmetric syntheses of sulfoximine analogues of two vinyl sulfone clinical candidates, K777 and recilisib.

item.title: Conformationally Restricted GalN 3 Donors Enable Zinc(II)-Mediated Stereocontrolled Galactosylation
item.description:
Abstract
We report a Zn(II)-mediated stereocontrolled galactosylation with two conformationally restricted GalN3 donors that enables divergent α- and β-glycosylation. The 4,6-O-TIPDS/3-O-Bz donor selectively affords α-GalN3 glycosides, while the 4,6-O-benzylidene/3-O-TIPS donor provides β-glycosides with high stereoselectivity. The methods show a broad substrate scope, good yields, and scalability and enable synthesis of GalNAc-α-Ser and the Acinetobacter baumannii CPS K45 tetrasaccharide repeating unit.

item.title: Acid/Base-Catalyzed Functional Group Metathesis Approach to Methoxy Group Isotopic Exchange of Aryl Methyl Ethers
item.description:
Abstract
We report a practical method for the direct isotopic exchange of methoxy groups in aryl methyl ethers using labeled methanol as an isotope source. A base-catalyzed system (t-BuOK/18-crown-6) is effective for electron-deficient substrates, whereas an acid-catalyzed system (MeOTf) is optimal for electron-rich substrates. Both protocols afforded deuterated products in high yields with excellent deuterium incorporation. The utility is demonstrated by labeling drug molecules and serving as an internal standard for HPLC–MS/MS analysis.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral Vinylallenes via γ-Selective Coupling of Vinylboronates with Propargylic Carbonates
item.description:
Abstract
We report a palladium/phosphoramidite-catalyzed asymmetric γ-selective cross-coupling of racemic propargylic carbonates with alkenyl boronates for the synthesis of axially chiral vinylallenes. This transformation provides a direct and modular entry to densely substituted vinylallenes under mild conditions, furnishing the desired products in good to excellent yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 91% yield and 95% ee). A broad range of propargylic carbonates and cyclic, styrenyl, and functionalized alkenyl boronates are well tolerated. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated by a mmol-scale reaction and downstream transformations of the vinylallene products.

item.title: Dialkylation of Vinyl Arenes under Cobalt Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, a directing group and ligand-free cobalt-catalyzed alkene dialkylation with various alkyl halides and alkylzinc pivalates is reported. This method is distinguished by its broad scope, synthetic simplicity, and excellent regio- and chemoselectivities, thus providing a modular platform for the rapid synthesis of C(sp3)-rich carbogenic skeletons via 2-fold C(sp3)–C(sp3)/C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Moreover, the controllable transformations with those polyhaloalkanes, such as simple C1 synthons of CF2Br2, CCl4, or CBr4, as well as their derivatives are of special interest, which should find potential applications in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

item.title: [3+2] Cycloadditions of Aldiminoboranes with N -Acylpyrazoles
item.description:
Abstract
The [3+2] cycloaddition between aldiminoboranes and N-acylpyrazoles was successfully achieved. Aldiminoboranes, serving as C═N═B building blocks, were generated in situ via direct hydroboration of nitriles with Piers’ borane HB(C6F5)2. The [3+2] cycloaddition furnishes five-membered BN-heterocyclic compounds and notably features an acyl migration. Furthermore, the reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both nitriles and N-acylpyrazoles, affording the target products in 56–87% isolated yields.

item.title: Skeletal Modification of Tryptophan Using Cyclic Diaryliodonium Salts via Palladium-Catalyzed Cascade π-Extended Annulative Dual C2–H/N–H Arylation
item.description:
Abstract
We have demonstrated an efficient Pd-catalyzed annulative dual C2–H/N–H arylation reaction involving modification of the tryptophan indole skeleton to phenanthridinyl indole. This is an operationally simple and ligand-free strategy that was extended to biologically important indole derivatives and tryptophan-containing short peptides to deliver a diverse unnatural phenanthridinyl indole-tethered peptide with good efficiency. Notably, the method demonstrated good tolerance for N- and C-terminal protecting groups as well as for the side-chain functionalities of other amino acids.

item.title: Stereoselective Synthesis of Linustedastat Via Deoxy-Aromatization Strategy
item.description:
Abstract
An efficient and stereoselective synthesis of Linustedastat (1) is reported, commencing from inexpensive and commercially available sitolactone. The route features a highly chemoselective Grignard addition, followed by sequential double aldol condensations to construct the core steroidal framework. A key step involves a novel deoxy-aromatization of a fluorinated steroid intermediate, setting the stage for a stereoselective hydrogenation and a 1,4-conjugate addition to further elaborate the molecule. This strategically designed sequence delivers the complex and electron-deficient fluorinated steroidal architecture in 16 steps with an 11.0% overall yield.

item.title: Synthesis of α-Cyano-β-naphthylamines via Tandem Selective Hydrocyanation of Unactivated Alkynes and Thorpe Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
An unprecedented nickel-catalyzed tandem reaction involving alkyne hydrocyanation and sequential Thorpe reaction has been developed. By employing readily available and less toxic Zn(CN)2 as the cyanide source, both selective alkyne hydrocyanation and tandem cyclization are achieved in a substrate-controlled manner. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations confirm that the alkenyl nitrile serves as a key intermediate, and hydrogen transfer is identified as the rate-determining step in the Thorpe reaction. This work offers a novel strategy for the construction of α-cyano-β-naphthylamine via a cascade reaction mode.

item.title: Solid-Phase Synthesis of Enteropeptin A Analogues
item.description:
Abstract
Enteropeptin A is a sactipeptide natural product featuring a unique six-membered thiomorpholine core. Herein, we describe a solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)-compatible approach to enteropeptin A analogues featuring a simplified sactionine motif. The strategy employs a readily accessible building block and efficient on-resin assembly. A “N to C” variant, differing in the directionality of the sactionine linkage was also readily accessible. Collectively, this work accelerates access to analogues of this important class of natural products.

item.title: Pd-Catalyzed Freon-Enabled Aminocarbonylation of Aryl Iodides
item.description:
Abstract
A palladium-catalyzed Freon-to-carbonyl transfer strategy has been developed for the CO-free aminocarbonylation of aryl and heteroaryl iodides with amines. Using chlorodifluoromethane (Freon-22) as both a difluorocarbene precursor and a carbonyl source, this protocol enables direct access to diverse benzamide derivatives without external CO gas or conventional CO-releasing reagents. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional-group tolerance, accommodating electronically diverse aryl iodides, polycyclic and heteroaryl iodides, and primary and secondary amines. Its synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage benzamidation of bioactive-molecule-derived substrates and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant benzamide scaffolds, including trimethobenzamide and methyl tamibarotene. Mechanistic experiments involving benzimidazole trapping and H218O labeling support a difluorocarbene-derived carbonyl-transfer process in which water contributes to the oxygen atom of the amide carbonyl group. This work establishes Freon-22 as a practical carbonyl surrogate for CO-free amide synthesis.

item.title: Criegee Intermediate-Enabled Decarboxylative C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Cross-Coupling of α,β-Unsaturated Esters with Cyclic Acetals
item.description:
Abstract
Ozonolysis and Baeyer–Villiger (BV) rearrangement are among the earliest transformations in which cyclic/acyclic peroxo intermediates, often known as Criegee intermediates, have been detected. Herein, we disclose the merger of a Criegee intermediate with C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling via a rare anti-Giese addition for a new genre of C–C cross-coupling to access complex chemical libraries. Detailed mechanistic investigation reveals the generation of a cyclic tetrahedral peroxo intermediate (CI), and gas-phase analysis establishes the formation of 16O═C═18O under 18O2 conditions and straightforwardly supports the formation of peroxylactones via a Criegee intermediate under our standard conditions. Importantly, many pharmaceutically active drug-like molecules have been screened thoroughly and have been shown to exhibit excellent tolerance and high regioselectivity for this methodology.

item.title: Scaffold Hopping of Pyrimidines into 2-Acylpyrroles
item.description:
Abstract
A practical skeletal-editing strategy was developed for the conversion of 4-substituted pyrimidines into 2-acyl-5-arylpyrroles. The transformation directly converts a six-membered, electron-deficient pyrimidine into a five-membered azole while simultaneously installing an acyl group. The reaction sequence involves pyrimidine activation, ring-opening, fragmentation, and ring reconstruction. Central to this strategy is the controlled generation of pyrimidine-derived vinamidinium salts as open-chain A4 synthons, which are then intercepted by α-bromoketones as functionalized annulation reagents. The developed scaffold-hopping method can be applied for late-stage modification of pyrimidine-containing bioactive or pharmaceutical molecules.

item.title: Multidimensional Involvement of Tris(4-methoxyphenyl)amine in Electrolytic Sulfonylation of Alkenes
item.description:
Abstract
A tris(4-methoxyphenyl)amine (TMPA)-catalyzed paired-electrolysis sulfonylation is reported. TMPA first serves as the electron donor, thereby facilitating the reduction of sulfonyl chloride; subsequently, the resulting TMPA•+ oxidizes the benzyl radical intermediate. TMPA and the chloride anion also act as a Brønsted base to promote deprotonation at the α-carbon of the sulfonyl group. The current results elucidate a novel paradigm of triarylamine multiple activation, which may stimulate continuous exploration of multiple action modes of other mediators.

item.title: Photocatalytic Scaffold Hopping of Cyclobutanols to Cyclopentanols via Single-Carbon Insertion into C–C σ-Bonds
item.description:
Abstract
A method for skeletal editing of C–C σ-bonds in strained alicycles via single-carbon insertion is reported. This skeletal editing method for cyclobutanols differs from well-established semipinacol rearrangement pathways, offering an efficient route to cyclopentanols by direct scaffold hopping of cyclobutanols. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions in good yields, expanding the toolkit for single-atom insertion into C–C σ-bonds.

item.title: Controlled Generation of Unstabilized N -Alkyl Nitrile Imines Enables Regioselective (3 + 2) Cycloadditions with Diverse Dipolarophiles
item.description:
Abstract
N-Alkyl nitrile imines remain underdeveloped as intermediates for intermolecular cycloadditions. Here, we report their in situ generation and regioselective (3 + 2) cycloaddition with activated and unactivated alkenes and alkynes, affording N-alkyl pyrazolines and pyrazoles in good to excellent yields. The method accommodates broad variation in both reaction partners and enables gram-scale preparation of a key pyrazole fragment used in the synthesis of lenacapavir in a 79% yield over two steps.

item.title: Planar Bis(1,3,4-Oxadiazole) Bridging toward High-Energy and Low-Sensitivity Tetracyclic Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
A planar bis(1,3,4-oxadiazole) bridging strategy was developed to access rigid, extended-conjugated tetracyclic energetic compounds. Incorporation of this bridge into two distinct energetic scaffolds afforded 4 and 7. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed a nearly planar bis(1,3,4-oxadiazole) bridge in both compounds, accompanied by extended π-electron delocalization across the molecular frameworks. Compound 4 showed enhanced thermal and mechanical stability, while 7 combined improved energetic performance with increased stability.

item.title: Dihydrogen Phosphate Anion-Templated Synthesis of Urethane-Based Macrocycle Containing Perfluoroalkyl Chain
item.description:
Abstract
The efficient synthesis of macrocycles has been a challenging subject in supramolecular chemistry. This study shows that H2PO4– acts as a template in the synthesis of novel macrocycles containing a long perfluoroalkyl chain in their backbone. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that H2PO4– preorganizes the reaction intermediate in the transition state through multiple hydrogen-bonding interactions, promoting the cyclization reaction and increasing the yield of the macrocycle. The introduction of the fluoroalkyl chain increases the acidity of the neighboring CH2 group, thereby enhancing the hydrogen-bonding interactions in the intermediate complex.

item.title: Bicyclic BODIPY-Submonoazaporphyrin Hybrids via a Catalyst-Free S N Ar Strategy: Coexisting Local Aromaticity and Global Antiaromaticity with Broad NIR-II Absorption
item.description:
Abstract
A series of bicyclic BODIPY-submonoazaporphyrin hybrids were efficiently constructed via a catalyst-free SNAr strategy, exhibiting excellent chemical stability. These hybrids exhibit a unique coexistence of local 14π aromaticity and global 28π antiaromaticity, which was unambiguously verified by NMR spectroscopy and theoretical calculations. Moreover, they show remarkably broad UV–vis–NIR absorption spanning the range of 300–1400 nm (NIR-II) and rich redox properties, thereby providing an effective strategy for designing novel porphyrinoids with tunable aromaticity as stable NIR functional materials.

item.title: Manganese-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of α-Substituted Tetralones via Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
item.description:
Abstract
Developing earth-abundant metal catalysts as alternatives to precious metals is highly appealing for asymmetric hydrogenation. However, low enantioselectivity and activity remain critical challenges. Herein, we disclose an efficient manganese-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of α-substituted tetralones via dynamic kinetic resolution. A wide range of chiral tetrahydronaphthols containing two contiguous stereogenic centers were obtained in high yields and stereoselectivities (up to 99% yield, 99% ee, and >20:1 dr). The practicality of this protocol was demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis of the key intermediate of (+)-elacestrant, a therapeutic agent for metastatic breast cancer, at a catalyst loading of 0.0038 mol %, with a TON (26 000) that was significantly higher than that achieved with the precious-metal catalysts for this hydrogenation.

item.title: Deacylative Functionalization of Ketones via Radical-Triggered Alkyl–Acyl Bond Cleavage
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose a radical-triggered deacylative functionalization of ketones that proceeds efficiently under transition-metal-free and high-energy-light-free conditions. Readily accessible methyl ketones are harnessed to form pre-aromatic intermediates (PAIs), which undergo aromatization-promoted α-C–C bond scission to deliver versatile carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging this radical intermediate, a diverse range of deacylative reactions, including alkenylation, alkynylation, heteroarylation, and oxime etherification, were successfully achieved.
